Mock Exam 1.q: A BA organizes an online order into Submission, Processing, and Delivery. Which Case Life Cycle building block do these represent?
o: Steps
Processes
Personas
Stages
Mock Exam 1.r: Stages divide the Case Life Cycle into high-level phases such as Submission, Processing, and Delivery. Within each Stage, Processes group the Steps that perform the actual work. Stages are the outermost container; Steps are the innermost

Mock Exam 1.q: A System Architect is reviewing a newly created Case Type in App Studio. The team lead asks why the first Stage — currently named 'Intake' — cannot be moved below the 'Review' Stage. What is the correct explanation?
o: Stage transitions are configured on it
It can be freely reordered like any Stage
It is the first Stage (green), cannot be deleted or repositioned, and assigns the Case ID on creation
It is the final Stage and is red
Mock Exam 1.r: The Create Stage is first (green bar), fixed in position (can be renamed), assigns the Case ID, and has no Stage transitions

Mock Exam 1.q: Every Case Type should have at least one of which Stage type, denoted by a red bar?
o: Alternate Stage
Primary Stage
Create Stage
Resolution Stage
Mock Exam 1.r: Resolution Stages, displayed with a red bar, mark the formal end of a Case Life Cycle — for example, Resolved-Completed or Resolved-Rejected. Every Case Type must include at least one Resolution Stage to ensure that Cases always reach a defined endpoint

Mock Exam 1.q: An SLA defines a goal of 4 hours and a deadline of 24 hours. What is true of these intervals?
o: The deadline is earlier than the goal
They are identical
The goal is the earlier 'should-complete-by' target; the deadline is the later 'must-complete-by' limit
The goal is optional
Mock Exam 1.r: In a Pega SLA, the Goal is the earlier 'should-complete-by' target and the Deadline is the later hard limit. As each threshold passes, Urgency increases automatically, pushing the Assignment higher in the operator's Worklist to signal overdue work

Mock Exam 1.q: A claims team needs an Assignment available to any qualified member to pull. Where should it route?
o: A specific user's Worklist
The customer
An Access Role
A Work Queue (shared)
Mock Exam 1.r: A Work Queue is a shared, pull-based pool where any qualified team member can claim and complete an Assignment. A Worklist, by contrast, routes to one specific named operator. Use a Work Queue for team-based routing and a Worklist for personal assignments

Mock Exam 1.q: Expense approvals must be signed off by the manager and then a director for larger amounts. Which pattern is this?
o: Single approval
A duplicate Case search
A Work Queue
Cascading approval (multiple sequential approvers / authority matrix)
Mock Exam 1.r: Cascading approval routes the same Assignment through multiple sequential approvers in order, each at a higher authority level — often defined by an authority matrix. The Case advances only after every level of the chain has signed off

Mock Exam 1.q: In a Search duplicate Cases Step, which condition type MUST match for a Case to be flagged?
o: An SLA condition
A weighted condition
A basic condition
An Access condition
Mock Exam 1.r: In a Search Duplicate Cases Step, Basic conditions are mandatory — all must match for a duplicate flag. Weighted conditions are optional; each carries a score and the total must reach a configured threshold. A duplicate is flagged only when at least one Basic condition matches

Mock Exam 1.q: Customers must be able to cancel a request at any point during the Case. How is this best configured?
o: A required Step in the Create Stage
An Automation Step that runs immediately
A Case-wide optional action
A Stage-wide optional action in the first Stage only
Mock Exam 1.r: A Case-wide optional action is available at any Stage of the Case, letting users trigger it regardless of the current flow step. Stage-wide optional actions, by contrast, are restricted to a single Stage and disappear from the Actions menu once the Case moves forward

Mock Exam 1.q: A System Architect is designing a loan application workflow. The 'Collateral Review' Stage should be skipped for loans under $50,000, and within that Stage, the 'Third-Party Appraisal' Process should be skipped if the applicant has a platinum credit rating. Which TWO statements correctly describe how to configure these skip conditions?
o: Configure a When Condition on the Stage to skip it when loan amount < $50,000
A single skip condition on the Stage automatically skips all its Processes as well
Configure a separate When Condition on the Process to skip it when credit rating = Platinum
Stage skip and Process skip must use the same When Condition to function correctly
Mock Exam 1.r: Stage-level and Process-level skip conditions are configured independently. A Stage skip bypasses the entire Stage; a Process skip only bypasses that Process within an active Stage.

Mock Exam 1.q: A System Architect is configuring a Collect Information Step for a Claims intake process. A colleague asks what element defines the user-facing form and controls which fields are displayed during an Assignment. What is the purpose of a Flow Action in a Process?
o: It authenticates the user
It deploys the application
It defines a user action/form that lets a user provide input to advance an Assignment
It stores data permanently
Mock Exam 1.r: A Flow Action defines the user-facing form attached to a Step, specifying which fields are shown and how user input advances the Case. It is the primary mechanism for collecting information from operators or customers during an Assignment

Mock Exam 1.q: A System Architect at GoGoRoad is designing a Roadside Assistance Case Type. The lead SA recommends creating child Cases for 'Tow Truck Dispatch' and 'Payment Processing'. Which TWO of the following justify using child Cases in this scenario?
o: Child Cases are required whenever a Case has more than three Stages
Each subprocess follows a different timeline and has its own SLA
Child Cases automatically copy all parent Case data without any configuration
Each subprocess is performed by a different party (dispatcher vs. billing team)
Mock Exam 1.r: Child Cases are appropriate when work is performed by different parties or follows different timelines.

Mock Exam 1.q: Which TWO are examples of Automation shapes (system actions) in a Process Flow?
o: Manually approve an expense
Require a user to type into a form
Change the Stage of a Case
Send an email / create a PDF
Mock Exam 1.r: Automation shapes execute system-level actions without requiring operator input — for example, sending emails, generating PDFs, changing the Case Stage, creating child Cases, or pausing on a timer. Collect Information shapes are the counterpart that requires user input

Mock Exam 1.q: A value-by-conditions decision with several possible outcomes is needed. Which construct fits best?
o: An SLA
A single true/false When Condition
A Decision Table (or Decision Tree)
A Work Queue
Mock Exam 1.r: A Decision Table evaluates rows of conditions against input values and returns one of many possible results. Unlike a When Condition, which only produces a true or false result, Decision Tables support multiple branches and are ideal for value-by-conditions logic with several outcomes

Mock Exam 1.q: A Business Architect is documenting role-based access for a Claims application. She notes that both junior and senior adjusters will access the same portal and share the same access rights. What is the correct term for this category of users in Pega?
o: A database table
A Ruleset version
A single named individual
A category/role of users who interact with a Case
Mock Exam 1.r: A Persona defines a category or role of users who interact with a Case — for example, Junior Adjuster. Multiple operators can share a single Persona, allowing the same access rights and UX to be configured once for the entire group rather than individually

Mock Exam 1.q: Two onboarding Processes can run in any order, and the Stage advances when both finish. How should they be configured?
o: As parallel Processes
As a single sequential Process
As Collect information Steps
As Alternate Stages
Mock Exam 1.r: Parallel Processes run simultaneously and independently within a Stage; the Stage does not advance until all of them complete. Sequential Processes, by contrast, run one after another in a defined order and each must finish before the next begins

Mock Exam 1.q: In App Studio a Customer 'data object' groups related 'fields'. What are these called in Dev Studio?
o: work group and operators
data type and properties
data page and records
class and rulesets
Mock Exam 1.r: Pega uses different terminology in each Studio: what App Studio calls a 'data object' is a 'data type' in Dev Studio, and what App Studio calls a 'field' is a 'property' in Dev Studio. The underlying artifacts are identical — only the labels change between studios

Mock Exam 1.q: A System Architect needs to ensure that user-entered data meets business rules before a Case can proceed. She wants to block invalid entries and display an error message. Which TWO options correctly describe how Pega validates data using business logic in App Studio?
o: Configure a Validation Condition on a specific Step to validate data at that Assignment
Field Type selection alone is sufficient to enforce all business rule validations
Business logic validation is always configured in Dev Studio only
Configure a Validation Condition on a Stage to block invalid data across multiple Steps
Mock Exam 1.r: App Studio supports both Stage-level and Step-level business logic validation conditions.

Mock Exam 1.q: A credit card expiration date must be in the future before the Case proceeds. What should a BA add?
o: A default value of today
A parallel Process
Business-logic validation checking the date is in the future
A Work Queue
Mock Exam 1.r: Validation rules enforce business logic at the point of data entry, blocking a Step from completing until the data meets the defined criteria. They prevent invalid values — such as a past credit-card expiration date — from being submitted and advancing the Case

Mock Exam 1.q: A System Architect is configuring a Data Page that loads customer records from an external CRM. She needs to decide the correct scope and refresh strategy. Which TWO statements about Data Page configuration are correct?
o: The refresh strategy only applies to Node-scope Data Pages, not Thread or Requestor scope
A Requestor-scope Data Page is shared across all Cases by all users on the node
A Thread-scope Data Page is unique to each Case instance and refreshes independently per Case
A Node-scope Data Page is shared by all users on the system and is ideal for common static data
Mock Exam 1.r: Node scope = shared by all users (common static data). Thread scope = unique per Case.

Mock Exam 1.q: A System Architect creates a new Customer data object in App Studio and wants to understand what Data Pages are available for use without any additional configuration. How many default Data Pages does each data object receive, and what types are they?
o: Three: single read-only, list read-only, single read-and-write
Two: single and list read-only
One: single read-and-write
Four including a savable page
Mock Exam 1.r: When a data object is created, Pega auto-generates three default Data Pages: a single read-only, a list read-only, and a single read-and-write (savable). Case Types receive only two (single and list, both read-only) because Cases are not saved or retrieved via Data Pages

Mock Exam 1.q: Which Data Page writes data back to its system of record (local or external)?
o: A Savable Data Page
A single read-only Data Page
A simulated Data Page
A list read-only Data Page
Mock Exam 1.r: A Savable Data Page is the only Data Page mode that persists data back to the System of Record. It uses a configured data save plan to write a single page or page list to a local data type or external connector, completing a read-then-write integration cycle

Mock Exam 1.q: An external integration is not ready, but development must continue. What is the best approach?
o: Use a simulated data source returning placeholder data
Convert the object to Embedded Data permanently
Hard-code values into every Case
Stop development until the API is live
Mock Exam 1.r: Simulated data sources let development continue with realistic placeholder data when an external integration is unavailable or unfinished. Once the real system is ready, the simulation is swapped for the live connector without requiring changes to the Case design

Mock Exam 1.q: Customers type credit-card details into each order; only one card per order. Which relationship configuration?
o: Data reference, List of records
Embedded Data, List of records
Case reference, Single record
Embedded Data, Single record
Mock Exam 1.r: Embedded Data stores information directly within the Case rather than in a separate data table or external system. Because the customer enters one credit card per order, the cardinality is Single record rather than a page list, making Embedded Data Single the correct configuration

Mock Exam 1.q: A System Architect must save user-edited customer contact data back to an external system of record using a savable Data Page. Which TWO statements correctly describe requirements for this configuration?
o: Setting Edit Mode to 'Editable' is sufficient — no save plan is needed
The save plan's connector option supports REST-based external saves only
The Data Page Edit Mode must be set to 'Savable'
The Save Data Page Step must be placed AFTER the Assignment where the user enters data
Mock Exam 1.r: Savable Data Pages require Edit Mode = Savable and a Save Data Page Step placed AFTER the user's Assignment.

Mock Exam 1.q: Stale data risks bad outcomes. What balances performance against data freshness for a Data Page?
o: A Work Queue
A refresh strategy
A default value
An Access Role
Mock Exam 1.r: A Data Page's refresh strategy controls when cached data is reloaded — options include once per interaction, do not reload, or reload if older than a specified interval. Choosing the right strategy avoids stale results while minimizing unnecessary calls to external systems

Mock Exam 1.q: A System Architect is modeling the relationship between a Loan Application Case Type and a Customer data object. She needs to understand what a data relationship artifact represents before deciding on the correct configuration. Which TWO statements about a data relationship are correct?
o: It can relate an object to a Case Type, object to object, or Case Type to Case Type
It replaces the need for data objects
It is a container that associates related fields but stores no data
It permanently stores the field values itself
Mock Exam 1.r: A data relationship is a structural link between a Case Type, data type, or another Case Type that describes how they relate. It does not hold data itself — the data lives in the connected objects. The relationship defines the association type and cardinality only

Mock Exam 1.q: A System Architect configures a data type to store customer records locally in Pega. After saving a record, a colleague asks why each record receives an auto-generated identifier automatically. What is a pyGUID for a locally-stored Data Record?
o: A simulated data source
The Case status
The customer's email
An auto-assigned unique identifier stored with the Case for later retrieval
Mock Exam 1.r: When a Data Record is saved locally, Pega auto-assigns a pyGUID — a unique identifier stored on the Case for later retrieval. It ensures every record is uniquely addressable without requiring the developer to configure a custom primary key

Mock Exam 1.q: A System Architect is explaining Rule resolution and inheritance to a new team member. Which TWO statements correctly describe how Pega resolves which Rule to apply at runtime?
o: Pattern inheritance automatically reuses Rules based on shared class-name prefixes
The Ruleset stack determines the version search order within a single class
Pega searches from the most-specific class upward through the class hierarchy
Directed inheritance requires a manual search path to be coded in Java
Mock Exam 1.r: Pega starts from the most-specific class and walks up via pattern (auto, prefix-based) then directed (explicit parent) inheritance D is partially correct but the primary resolution is class-based first

Mock Exam 1.q: A reusable rule built in Dev Studio must be available for assembly in the App Studio Case Designer. What is required?
o: Convert it to an Access Role
Move it to the Implementation Layer
Mark it as a relevant record
Delete it from Dev Studio
Mock Exam 1.r: Marking a Dev Studio rule as a relevant record exposes it to App Studio's Case Designer, allowing business-level authors to select and configure it without accessing Dev Studio. Rules not marked as relevant remain invisible to App Studio users

Mock Exam 1.q: A System Architect is configuring a new application and needs to understand version control. She creates a Ruleset named 'Claims' with version 01-02-03. A colleague asks what these three number segments represent. What is the correct explanation?
o: Major 01, minor 02, patch 03
Version 1023
Three separate Rulesets
A date
Mock Exam 1.r: A Ruleset version number has three two-digit segments: major (01), minor (02), and patch (03). The major segment represents breaking changes, minor indicates feature additions, and patch covers small fixes. Pega locks all three segments to exactly two digits each

Mock Exam 1.q: A System Architect is explaining rule inheritance to a new team member. She notes that one type of inheritance requires no explicit configuration because it is determined automatically by how the class is named. Which inheritance type is automatic and based on the class-name prefix?
o: Multiple inheritance
Pattern inheritance
Manual inheritance
Directed inheritance
Mock Exam 1.r: Pattern inheritance automatically searches parent classes by stripping the last prefix segment from the class name — for example, TGB-IT-Work inherits from TGB-IT. Directed inheritance is explicitly configured on the class form to reach classes outside the naming hierarchy, such as standard Pega classes

Mock Exam 1.q: Which capability gives one operator a private space whose changes stay hidden until shared to a Branch?
o: A Workspace
A Work Queue
An Access Group
A Ruleset
Mock Exam 1.r: A Workspace is tied to one operator and one application; changes are private until shared to a Branch

Mock Exam 1.q: A team lead asks a System Architect to explain the roles of Workspaces and Branches in Pega team development. Which TWO statements correctly describe their relationship?
o: A Workspace is a private development space tied to one operator and one application
Changes in a Workspace stay private until shared to a Branch to avoid rule conflicts
A Branch can be shared by multiple operators working on the same application simultaneously
Workspaces automatically merge into the main application when the operator logs out
Mock Exam 1.r: Workspaces are private per-operator; changes share to a Branch when ready.

Mock Exam 1.q: Which class type contains the rules that describe how to PROCESS Cases?
o: The Integration class
The Access class
The Work class
The Data class
Mock Exam 1.r: The Work class holds rules that govern how Cases are created, processed, and resolved. The Integration class contains connector rules for communicating with external systems. The Data class defines data types and their properties. Each class serves a distinct architectural purpose

Mock Exam 1.q: A System Architect is preparing a compliance report on the accessibility features built into Pega Platform's Constellation architecture. Which TWO accessibility features does Constellation provide automatically without additional developer configuration?
o: Section 508 compliance for US government applications
Automatic translation of all text into 50+ languages
WCAG 2.1 compliance built into Constellation patterns
Manual keyboard shortcut configuration per field
Mock Exam 1.r: Constellation's Center-out architecture embeds WCAG 2.1 and Section 508 compliance into its core patterns. When accessibility standards update, a central change propagates automatically. Language translation and keyboard shortcuts require separate configuration

Mock Exam 1.q: A lightweight tool inside App Studio for capturing user stories, bugs, and feedback in real time is:
o: Agile Studio
Prediction Studio
Deployment Manager
Agile Workbench
Mock Exam 1.r: Agile Workbench is a lightweight backlog tool embedded directly in App Studio for capturing user stories, bugs, and feedback in real time alongside Case design. Agile Studio is the separate, full-featured Pega application for managing sprints, releases, and teams at scale

Mock Exam 1.q: A user logs in with username, password, and a one-time code. This is:
o: Authorization
Authentication
A Data Transform
A Decision Table
Mock Exam 1.r: Authentication validates who the user is by checking credentials, tokens, or MFA codes at login. Authorization is a subsequent, separate step that determines what the verified user is permitted to access and perform, enforced through their Access Roles

Mock Exam 1.q: Which artifact defines WHAT actions/classes a user is permitted to use (the permissions)?
o: Access Role
Operator record
Access Group
Persona
Mock Exam 1.r: An Access Role specifies the precise permissions a user has — which classes, actions, and rules they can use. Access Groups bundle one or more roles with an application and its portals, forming the complete operator profile that is granted at login

Mock Exam 1.q: Which ties an operator to an application, portals, a default work group, and Access Roles?
o: Access Role
Access Group
Work Queue
Data Transform
Mock Exam 1.r: An Access Group links an operator to a specific application, one or more portal layouts, a default work group, and one or more Access Roles. It is the primary artifact that determines what a user sees and can do at runtime in a Pega application

Mock Exam 1.q: A junior developer asks about the distinction between two fundamental security layers in Pega Platform. He wants to know which layer verifies WHO a user is, and which layer controls WHAT that user can access. Which sequence is correct?
o: Neither is needed if a Persona exists
Authorization first, then authentication
Both occur only after the Case resolves
Authentication first (verify identity), then authorization (grant access by role)
Mock Exam 1.r: Authentication always comes first — verifying the user's identity via credentials or MFA before granting entry. Authorization follows — evaluating the user's Access Roles to determine which classes, actions, and rules they are permitted to use within the application

Mock Exam 1.q: Before going live with a new Pega application, a Lead System Architect directs the team to run the Security Checklist in Dev Studio. A junior developer asks why this step is important beyond standard code review. What is the primary purpose of the Security Checklist?
o: To create Insights
To route Assignments
To guide hardening the application against security risks before go-live
To calculate field values
Mock Exam 1.r: The Security Checklist in Dev Studio lists recommended hardening tasks — such as enabling TLS, removing default accounts, and locking Rulesets — to reduce attack surface before go-live. Each item shows a pass or fail status and provides remediation guidance

Mock Exam 1.q: Role-based access control (RBAC) in Pega is implemented primarily through which pairing?
o: Work Queues and Worklists
Data Pages and Data Transforms
Access Groups and Access Roles
Branches and Rulesets
Mock Exam 1.r: Role-Based Access Control in Pega assigns permissions to roles rather than individuals. Access Roles define class and action permissions; Access Groups bundle those roles with an application and portals; operators are then placed into the Access Group matching their job function

Mock Exam 1.q: A UX designer is configuring a Claims portal and needs to identify which View types in Pega Platform are always read-only and cannot be set to allow user edits. Which TWO View types are always read-only?
o: Form View
Edit View
Full Page View
Partial View
Mock Exam 1.r: Full Page Views and Partial Views in Pega Constellation are always read-only and cannot be configured to allow user edits — they are designed purely for display. Form Views and Edit Views are editable, making them the correct choice for data-entry Steps in a Case Life Cycle.

Mock Exam 1.q: A System Architect adds a new Collect Information Step to a Case Life Cycle in App Studio and clicks 'Configure View'. She notices a new Form View was created automatically. In which scenario does Pega Platform automatically create a Form View?
o: When you designate Primary Fields
When you Configure View for a Step on the Workflow tab
When you run a Case
When you open the Summary panel
Mock Exam 1.r: When a System Architect clicks 'Configure View' on a Collect Information Step in the Workflow tab, Pega automatically creates a Form View using the Default form template. Views created elsewhere — such as the UX tab — are not auto-generated and must be built manually

Mock Exam 1.q: A UX designer is configuring dynamic behavior on a Claims portal. She wants certain fields to appear only when a checkbox is selected, and she wants to reuse the same condition across multiple Views. Which TWO options correctly describe how to implement this in Pega?
o: Use a Custom Condition for a simple, one-time visibility condition on a single field
Use a When Rule for complex conditions that need to be reused across multiple Views
When Rules are automatically applied to all fields in the application without configuration
Custom Conditions support Java expressions and can be shared across applications
Mock Exam 1.r: When Rules are reusable across the application; Custom Conditions are simple one-off expressions.

Mock Exam 1.q: A BA has marked the 'Policy Number' and 'Claim Date' fields as Primary Fields on a Claims Case Type. She asks the SA where these fields will automatically appear without any additional configuration. Where are Primary Fields automatically displayed?
o: Only in Dev Studio
On the default Create, Edit, and Details Views
On the List View only
Only on the Pulse View
Mock Exam 1.r: Primary Fields are designated on the Case Type's Data Model tab. Once marked, they automatically appear on the Create, Edit, and Details Views without any additional configuration, ensuring the most important fields are visible at the key points in the Case life cycle

Mock Exam 1.q: A System Architect has completed a Constellation portal for GoGoRoad and must now adapt it for Spanish-speaking users in Mexico. She needs to generate a translation package, send it for translation, and re-import it. Which two elements are NOT automatically included in the Pega translation package and must be handled separately?
o: Field labels and button text
Case status labels and error messages
Paragraph Rules (step instructions)
Data Page-sourced control text
Mock Exam 1.r: Step instructions stored in Paragraph Rules and text sourced from Data Pages are not auto-extracted into the Pega translation ZIP. Paragraph Rules must be edited manually inside the translated ruleset folder; Data Page text must be added via App Studio → Settings → Localization → Additional text. Field labels, button text, case status labels, and error messages are all included automatically in the translation package.

Mock Exam 1.q: A field should appear only when a condition is true. What drives this dynamic visibility?
o: A Ruleset version
The number of operators
A visibility condition (visible-when / When rule)
The portal theme
Mock Exam 1.r: A visibility condition — implemented as a When rule — evaluates field values at run time and shows or hides a UI element based on the result. This keeps forms clean and reduces user error by surfacing fields only when they are contextually relevant

Mock Exam 1.q: Which design-time capability suggests Case Types, Data Model fields, and Personas as you build in App Studio?
o: Search Assistant
Pega GenAI Autopilot
Pega GenAI Coach
Knowledge Buddy
Mock Exam 1.r: Pega GenAI Autopilot assists architects at design time by suggesting Case Types, data fields, and Personas as the application is built in App Studio. Pega GenAI Coach operates at run time, providing end users with task-specific guidance while they work on open Cases

Mock Exam 1.q: A Solutions Consultant is presenting Pega Blueprint to a client stakeholder who is unfamiliar with Pega Platform. The stakeholder asks whether Blueprint requires a Pega Platform license to use collaboratively during the design phase. Which statement about Pega Blueprint is correct?
o: It fully replaces App Studio
It is LSA-only
It requires PremBridge to import
It is a standalone SaaS tool that needs no Pega login to collaborate and augments App Studio
Mock Exam 1.r: Pega Blueprint is a standalone SaaS tool that requires no Pega Platform license, so stakeholders can collaborate on application design without a Pega login. It augments App Studio — designs are imported for refinement — but does not replace it, and no bridge license is needed to import

Mock Exam 1.q: A business stakeholder at an insurance company wants users to be able to ask natural-language questions about internal policy documents directly within the Pega application. Which Pega GenAI feature should the System Architect implement?
o: A duplicate Case search
A CI/CD pipeline
A Decision Table editor
A conversational tool giving instant answers from the org's procedural docs and knowledge bases
Mock Exam 1.r: Pega Knowledge Buddy is a conversational AI tool that answers natural-language questions by searching the organization's own documents, policies, and knowledge bases. It delivers client-specific, contextual answers within the Pega application without requiring users to switch to external search tools

Mock Exam 1.q: A Connect Generative AI Step returns long, complex JSON. Per best practice, map it to which Field Type?
o: Currency
Date only
Boolean
Text (paragraph)
Mock Exam 1.r: Generative AI responses are often unstructured prose, so mapping the output to a Text (paragraph) property preserves the full content without truncation. Single-value fields are too narrow for long text, and page lists require structured JSON — Text (paragraph) is the best fit for unstructured GenAI output

Mock Exam 1.q: Which run-time capability provides expert, task-specific guidance to end users on a Case?
o: Pega GenAI Coach
OpenAI search
Pega GenAI Autopilot
Pega Blueprint
Mock Exam 1.r: Pega GenAI Coach runs at case-processing time, providing operators with expert, task-specific guidance on the current assignment. Blueprint and Autopilot are design-time tools — Blueprint proposes the initial application structure, and Autopilot accelerates configuration inside App Studio

Mock Exam 1.q: A System Architect is evaluating Pega GenAI Agents for a customer-service automation project. The client wants to know what actions an Agent can perform during a conversation, particularly when Tool Rules are configured to govern its behavior. Which TWO are capabilities of Pega GenAI Agents with Tool Rules?
o: Run automations, start Cases, call other agents, launch user actions
Replace all security and compliance controls
Compile the application's Java source
Extract data from uploaded documents during a conversation
Mock Exam 1.r: Pega GenAI Agents can execute automations — starting Cases, running RPA, calling other agents — and can extract data from uploaded documents during a conversation. Tool Rules extend what an Agent can do while enforcing organizational governance and security boundaries

Mock Exam 1.q: Which Pega tool provides a model-driven CI/CD pipeline to promote changes across environments?
o: Agile Workbench
Pega Deployment Manager
Prediction Studio
Pega Robot Manager
Mock Exam 1.r: Pega Deployment Manager provides a model-driven CI/CD pipeline that automates the promotion of application changes across environments — from development through QA and staging to production — without requiring custom DevOps scripting or manual deployments

Mock Exam 1.q: A System Architect is debugging a Case that routes incorrectly after a Decision shape. She needs to trace the exact property values and rule execution order at runtime without modifying the application code. Which Pega Platform tool should she use?
o: The Tracer, which logs rule execution steps and property value changes in real time
The UI Inspector, which provides CSS and component structure but no runtime logic tracing
The Clipboard, which shows the current data state but does not trace rule execution order
The Xray tool, which shows field-level security and page structure but not flow execution
Mock Exam 1.r: The Tracer is the correct tool for runtime debugging — it logs every rule executed, every property changed (highlighted in yellow), and the execution path through a flow. The Clipboard, Xray, and UI Inspector serve different purposes and do not trace flow execution order

Mock Exam 1.q: A DevOps engineer is building a CI/CD pipeline using Pega Deployment Manager. The team lead asks which two categories of automated tests should be included to validate changes before they are promoted to the next environment. Which TWO test types help ensure successful application deployment?
o: Automated unit tests of rules/logic
Scenario (end-to-end) tests of the workflow
Manual re-typing of all data
Deleting the test environment
Mock Exam 1.r: Automated unit tests validate individual rules and logic in isolation, while scenario (end-to-end) tests verify that complete Case workflows behave correctly. Running both types in the CI/CD pipeline catches regressions early and ensures changes are safe to promote to the next environment

Mock Exam 1.q: A business manager wants to create a visual report showing the number of open Claims by region, save it for daily review, and share it with her team through a portal landing page. What Pega Platform feature enables this?
o: A CI/CD pipeline
An Access Role
A Ruleset version
A saved data query rendered as a table or chart that can be shared between users
Mock Exam 1.r: Insights are saved data queries rendered as interactive tables or charts within Pega Platform. They can be shared with team members and embedded on portal landing pages, giving business managers repeatable access to operational reports without requiring custom development

Mock Exam 1.q: Where in App Studio do you explore application data and build Insights?
o: Admin Studio
Prediction Studio
The Records tab
The Explore Data landing page
Mock Exam 1.r: The Explore Data landing page in App Studio is the entry point for all in-platform data analysis. Users can browse application data objects, run ad-hoc queries, and build and save Insights from the results — all without leaving the low-code environment

Mock Exam 1.q: Which tool EXTRACTS Pega data to external systems for analysis outside Pega?
o: The Explore Data landing page
BIX (Business Intelligence Exchange)
A table Insight
A chart Insight
Mock Exam 1.r: Business Intelligence Exchange (BIX) is the Pega tool for extracting application data into flat files or external databases, enabling analysis in third-party BI platforms. Insights, by contrast, create visualizations and saved queries that remain inside the Pega application

Mock Exam 2.q: Within a Stage, related Steps users complete are grouped into which building block?
o: A Stage
A Persona
A Channel
A Process
Mock Exam 2.r: A Process groups Steps within a Stage; a Case can move to the next Process after the current one completes

Mock Exam 2.q: A Collect information Step (user action) is shown in the Case Life Cycle with which icon color?
o: Blue
Red
Green
Yellow
Mock Exam 2.r: Steps that require user input are Collect Information Steps, displayed in green in the Case Life Cycle Designer. Steps that run automatically as system actions are Automation Steps, displayed in yellow. The color coding makes the Case design readable at a glance

Mock Exam 2.q: A Case must pause until the first business day of next month, then continue. Which Wait type fits?
o: A case-dependency Wait
A Decision Table
A timer Wait (until a date/time)
A cascading approval
Mock Exam 2.r: A timer Wait Step pauses the Case until a specific date and time is reached, then automatically continues. A case-dependency Wait pauses the parent Case until one or more child or sibling Cases reach a specified status. Both types suspend flow without user interaction

Mock Exam 2.q: Which automation Step transitions a Case to a specific Stage automatically (often to/from Alternate Stages)?
o: Change Stage automation
Collect information Step
Submit on the Create Stage
Persona Step
Mock Exam 2.r: The Change Stage Automation shape transitions the active Case to a target Stage without any user action. It is commonly used to jump to an Alternate Stage when an exception is detected, or to return to the primary path after an exception is resolved

Mock Exam 2.q: A System Architect is configuring SLAs for a Claims Case Type. The lead SA requires urgency to increase as milestones are missed and escalation actions to fire on each passed deadline interval. Which TWO statements about SLA configuration are correct?
o: Goal and deadline escalation actions can fire multiple times on each interval repeat
The passed deadline interval can repeat a fixed number of times or until the Assignment is completed
The passed deadline interval is configured in App Studio on the same form as goal and deadline
Urgency increases defined on a Stage-level SLA affect Case Urgency, not Assignment Urgency
Mock Exam 2.r: The passed deadline interval can repeat (count-based or until complete) and Stage-level Urgency adjustments affect Case Urgency.

Mock Exam 2.q: How many promoted Actions does a Case Type support, and where does it appear?
o: Two, on the Create Stage
Unlimited, in the Summary panel
One, as a button on the Case header
Three, in the Pulse feed
Mock Exam 2.r: A Case Type can have only one promoted Action — the first Case-wide optional action configured on the Case Type. It appears as a prominent button on the Case header, making it immediately visible to operators throughout the entire Case life cycle

Mock Exam 2.q: A System Architect is configuring a cascading approval for an expense report that requires sign-off from both a reporting manager and the Finance department head (who is outside the management hierarchy). Which TWO statements correctly describe the appropriate configuration?
o: The authority matrix's Decision table must be set to 'Evaluate all rows' to return all approvers
A reporting structure automatically includes people outside the org chart
Use an authority matrix, not a reporting structure, because Finance is outside the hierarchy
Setting 'Evaluate all rows' on the Decision table is optional for authority matrix approvals
Mock Exam 2.r: Use an authority matrix when approvers are outside the reporting structure. The Decision table MUST be set to Evaluate all rows — otherwise it returns only the first match and the cascade is incomplete.

Mock Exam 2.q: A 'Add note' action should be available only while the Case is in the Verification Stage. Configure it as:
o: A required Step in Create
A Case-wide optional action
An Automation Step
A Stage-wide optional action in Verification
Mock Exam 2.r: Stage-wide optional actions are available only while the Case is in a specific Stage. They appear in the Actions menu within that Stage and are hidden once the Case moves to another Stage. Case-wide optional actions remain available throughout the entire Case

Mock Exam 2.q: A System Architect is configuring conditional logic to skip a Verification Stage when a Claim is under $500. A new team member asks about the structure of a When Condition before assisting with the configuration. Which are the THREE elements of a When Condition Rule?
o: Input value, comparator, value to compare against
Operator, role, group
Stage, Process, Step
Goal, deadline, urgency
Mock Exam 2.r: A When Condition Rule has exactly three parts: the input value (a property), a comparator (equals, greater than, contains, etc.), and the comparison value. When the expression evaluates to true, the condition fires and the associated branch or rule executes

Mock Exam 2.q: A SLA's urgency should rise as work ages. When does urgency increase?
o: Only when the Case is created
At the goal and again at the deadline
Only after resolution
Never; urgency is fixed
Mock Exam 2.r: An SLA rule automatically increases an Assignment's Urgency value when the goal threshold passes and again when the deadline threshold passes. Higher Urgency ranks the Assignment closer to the top of the operator's Worklist, signaling it needs immediate attention

Mock Exam 2.q: A Lead System Architect is reviewing a proposed Case design for an onboarding application and recommends splitting some work into child Cases. She needs to justify the architectural decision to the business stakeholder. Which TWO are valid justifications for creating child Cases?
o: Eliminate the need for any data
Run work in parallel with independent ownership/SLAs
Remove the parent Case
Decompose complex work into focused, reusable Case Types
Mock Exam 2.r: Child Cases are appropriate when work must be decomposed into independently trackable units — for example, when parallel work streams need separate owners and SLAs, or when a sub-process is reusable across multiple parent Case Types for modularity and specialization

Mock Exam 2.q: A two-way branch: orders over $1,000 go to manager review, else auto-approve. Simplest construct?
o: A multi-outcome Decision Table is mandatory
An SLA goal
A When Condition (true/false)
A Work Queue assignment
Mock Exam 2.r: A When Condition (true/false) is the lightest-weight branching construct for a two-path decision. When there are more than two possible outcomes or complex value-matching is needed, a Decision Table or Decision Tree is the more appropriate construct

Mock Exam 2.q: A System Architect creates a new Case Type for a Loan Application and examines the Case Life Cycle in App Studio. She notices a Process was automatically added to the Create Stage without any manual configuration. What is the default Create Process added to the Create Stage?
o: A Partial View
A List View
A Multi-step Form
A Hierarchical Form
Mock Exam 2.r: When a new Case Type is created, Pega automatically adds a Multi-step Form as the default Create Process in the Create Stage. Architects can replace or supplement it with additional Steps based on the specific data-collection requirements of the application

Mock Exam 2.q: A System Architect is designing a complex Claims workflow. She needs to add a step that evaluates a claim amount against coverage tiers to automatically route the Case to one of three paths: Standard Review, Senior Review, or Escalated Review. Which TWO shapes should she use?
o: A Flow Action to determine which path the Case should follow automatically
A Decision shape (orange diamond) to create conditional paths in the process
A Wait Step to pause until the routing tier is determined
A Decision Table Rule to evaluate the claim amount and return the appropriate routing path
Mock Exam 2.r: A Decision shape adds conditional branching to a Process and can reference a Decision Table to evaluate the claim amount and return the path.

Mock Exam 2.q: Which naming convention is correct for a Step inside the 'Process order' Process?
o: Processing
Check inventory (verb + noun)
Inventory
Financial operations
Mock Exam 2.r: Pega naming conventions recommend verb + noun for Processes and Steps (e.g., 'Process order', 'Check inventory') to describe the action being taken. Stages should use a noun or gerund (e.g., 'Processing', 'Delivery') to describe the phase the Case is in

Mock Exam 2.q: Which model is the Conceptual Data Model translated and refined for Pega, using data objects and fields?
o: Physical Data Model
Integration Map
Conceptual Data Model
Logical Data Model
Mock Exam 2.r: The Logical Data Model is the Pega-specific translation of the Conceptual Data Model. Conceptual entities become data objects and their attributes become fields. This model defines the business-level data structure within the Pega application, independent of technical storage details

Mock Exam 2.q: Shipping cost depends on region and weight across several tiers. Which rule computes it cleanly?
o: A single default value
A Wait Step
An Access Group
A Decision Table
Mock Exam 2.r: A Decision Table evaluates rows of conditions — such as region and weight tier — against input values and returns the result of the first matching row. This makes it ideal for tiered pricing or categorization rules that would be complex to express with nested If/Else logic

Mock Exam 2.q: Most new Cases use Country = 'USA'. To save typing, configure the field with:
o: A calculated value
Validation rejecting other countries
A Data Transform that deletes the field
A default value of 'USA' (overridable)
Mock Exam 2.r: Configuring a default value pre-fills the field automatically when the form opens, reducing data-entry effort for common scenarios. Unlike a read-only calculated value, a default is editable — users can change it when the specific Case requires a different value

Mock Exam 2.q: A user selects from a list of existing Service Cases. Which relationship field type?
o: Case reference
Data reference
Embedded Data
Picklist
Mock Exam 2.r: A Case reference field lets the user select an existing Case as the data source — for example, linking a Service Case to its originating Sales Case. The relationship tracks the link without copying data, so the reference always points to the live source Case

Mock Exam 2.q: A System Architect is building a vehicle data feature. The Vehicle data object is not yet built, but she needs to reference it in the Case Life Cycle now. Which TWO statements correctly describe how to handle this in App Studio?
o: A Draft data object automatically completes its configuration when the Case is first run
Pega can create a Draft (placeholder) data object so the life cycle design can progress
Draft data objects are visible only in Dev Studio, not in App Studio
The Draft data object has no fields or integration settings and must be completed later
Mock Exam 2.r: Draft data objects are placeholders — they have no fields or integration settings but allow the Case Life Cycle design to proceed. The SA completes them later on the Data Objects landing page or in Dev Studio.

Mock Exam 2.q: A System Architect creates a new Case Type and wants to understand which Data Pages are auto-generated so she can use them when configuring a Case reference relationship in another Case Type. Case Types have how many default Data Pages, and what kind are they?
o: One read-write
Two, both read-only
None
Three, including read-write
Mock Exam 2.r: When a Case Type is created, Pega auto-generates two read-only Data Pages — a single-record and a list — used when another Case Type references this Case Type via a Case reference. Unlike data objects, no read-write default is generated because Cases are not saved via Data Pages

Mock Exam 2.q: A System Architect is configuring calculated fields for a GoGoRoad Claims Case Type. She needs to calculate total repair cost (sum of parts + labor) and auto-populate the claim status. Which TWO statements about calculated fields are correct?
o: Calculated fields are read-only — users cannot overwrite the derived value
Calculated fields are always stored in the database immediately upon computation
A calculated field can use a Decision Table as its source to return different values based on conditions
Marking a field 'calculated' automatically creates a When Rule to protect it from user edits
Mock Exam 2.r: Calculated fields are system-maintained and read-only to prevent overwriting. They can source from functions, expressions, or Decision Tables.

Mock Exam 2.q: A user enters quantities for many products in one order; products come from an external DB. The Order line added to the order is:
o: Embedded Data, List of records
Embedded Data, Single record
Data reference, Single record
Case reference, List of records
Mock Exam 2.r: When order-line quantities are entered directly in the Case (not from an external System of Record) and there are many lines per order, the relationship is Embedded Data with a List cardinality. The data lives inside the Case, not in a separate table or external system

Mock Exam 2.q: Which Field Type best enforces a fixed set of options like Standard/Express/Overnight?
o: Boolean
Attachment
Picklist
Text (free entry)
Mock Exam 2.r: A Picklist Field Type presents the user with a predefined set of choices and prevents any other values from being submitted. This enforces data quality for fields with a fixed vocabulary, such as shipping priority levels (Standard, Express, Overnight)

Mock Exam 2.q: Parent and child Cases must keep a shared reference value identical as it changes. Which mechanism?
o: An SLA
A validation rule
A Data Transform that propagates the value
A default value on each Case
Mock Exam 2.r: A Data Transform can copy and synchronize a shared reference field from a parent Case into one or more child Cases. When the parent value changes and the Data Transform is re-run, child Cases receive the updated value, maintaining data consistency across related work items

Mock Exam 2.q: A System Architect is modeling the data for a Loan Application Case Type. She must decide whether to use Embedded Data or a Data reference for the Applicant contact details. Which TWO statements correctly distinguish Embedded Data from a Data reference?
o: Data reference is sourced from local/external SOR Data Records
Both store data identically in the relationship
Embedded Data is sourced from user input directly in the Case
Embedded vs Data reference is decided by single vs list
Mock Exam 2.r: The key distinction between Embedded Data and Data reference is the data source. Embedded Data collects user input directly in the Case; Data reference reads from a local or external System of Record. Cardinality (single vs. list) is a secondary decision made after choosing the source

Mock Exam 2.q: Where can a BA enter Data Records locally without touching the database directly?
o: The Integration Map
The Records tab
Dev Studio only
The Pulse feed
Mock Exam 2.r: The Records tab in App Studio allows users to enter and manage Data Records stored in Pega-managed database tables without direct database access. Each record is automatically assigned a unique pyGUID as a persistent identifier for later retrieval

Mock Exam 2.q: In the Situational Layer Cake, where do enterprise-wide reusable assets (e.g., company-wide authentication) belong?
o: Division Layer
Implementation Layer
Application Layer
Enterprise Layer
Mock Exam 2.r: In the Situational Layer Cake, the Enterprise Layer is the foundation and contains organization-wide reusable assets — such as shared authentication rules, corporate branding, or common utilities. These assets are inherited by every division and application built on top of this layer

Mock Exam 2.q: A System Architect must configure version control and Ruleset management for a new Claims application being developed by a team of five architects. Which TWO statements correctly describe Pega's approach to Ruleset versioning?
o: Each Ruleset version can only contain Rules from a single class
The Ruleset stack determines the class hierarchy search order for Rule resolution
A new Ruleset version should be created whenever Case behavior must change, preserving the history
Older Ruleset versions should be locked to prevent accidental edits to released Rules
Mock Exam 2.r: New Ruleset versions capture behavior changes while preserving history; locking older versions prevents regression.

Mock Exam 2.q: Which inheritance is explicitly specified on the class form and reaches standard Pega classes like Work-?
o: Automatic inheritance
Directed inheritance
Ruleset inheritance
Pattern inheritance
Mock Exam 2.r: Directed inheritance is configured explicitly on the class form, pointing to a specific parent class regardless of the class name. This allows a business class to inherit from standard Pega classes such as Work- or Data-, which lie outside the business naming prefix hierarchy

Mock Exam 2.q: A new System Architect asks why there are so many types of Rules in Pega Platform and how they relate to the underlying structure. Her mentor explains the connection between a Rule and a Rule Type. What is the relationship between a Rule and a Rule Type in Pega Platform?
o: A Rule Type stores data values
A Rule is an instance of a Rule Type that determines the modeled behavior
They are unrelated
A Rule Type is one instance of a Rule
Mock Exam 2.r: A Rule Type is the template that defines what a rule does; a Rule is a concrete instance of that template. For example, the Flow Rule Type models Process behavior — every Flow rule in an application is a specific, named instance of that Rule Type configured for a particular purpose

Mock Exam 2.q: What enables a business user to update Case behavior (e.g., an approval threshold) without an application change request?
o: A Wait Step
Directed inheritance
Locking the Ruleset
Delegating the Rule to business users
Mock Exam 2.r: Delegation exposes a specific Rule — such as an SLA threshold or Decision Table — to business users in a simplified editor. They can change values without filing an IT change request. Only the delegated rule is editable; the rest of the application remains under controlled access

Mock Exam 2.q: A Scrum Master asks the SA to describe the Branch quality metrics she should monitor before approving a merge to the main application. Which TWO are documented Branch quality metrics in Pega Platform?
o: Number of active Workspaces on the Branch — indicates team size
Total Merge Conflicts — identifies potential conflicts to resolve before merging
Guardrails Weighted Score — indicates compliance with Pega best practices
Ruleset version number — indicates which version will be promoted
Mock Exam 2.r: The four documented Branch quality metrics are: Guardrails Weighted Score, Merge Conflicts, Test Coverage/Unit Tests, and Uncovered Rules. Ruleset version number and active Workspace count are not Branch quality metrics

Mock Exam 2.q: A development team is creating Rulesets for a new Claims application and proposes several names. The Lead System Architect reviews the list and asks the team to confirm they followed Pega naming guidelines before proceeding. Which of the following is a valid Ruleset naming best practice?
o: Use meaningful names ≤32 chars and avoid the 'Pega' prefix
Prefer cryptic acronyms
Always prefix with 'Pega-'
Use spaces and dashes freely
Mock Exam 2.r: Ruleset names must be meaningful and concise (32 characters or fewer). The 'Pega' and 'Pega-' prefixes are reserved for platform Rulesets and must never be used by application teams. Spaces and special characters are disallowed as they can cause rule-resolution errors

Mock Exam 2.q: A compliance officer asks a System Architect to confirm that the new Pega Constellation portal meets US federal accessibility requirements. Which standard does Pega's Constellation architecture comply with for US government applications?
o: Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act
WCAG 3.0 (not yet finalized)
GDPR Article 25 privacy by design
ISO/IEC 27001 information security standard
Mock Exam 2.r: Pega's Constellation architecture is built to comply with both WCAG 2.1 and Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act (the US federal accessibility standard). Compliance is embedded in the core patterns so developers do not need to add it manually

Mock Exam 2.q: A reusable feature is encapsulated so it can be stacked under other applications. This is a:
o: Decision Tree
Module application
Work Queue
Savable Data Page
Mock Exam 2.r: A module application encapsulates a specific reusable feature — such as a shared authentication flow — that can be stacked under other applications. Built-on applications inherit the module's rules, allowing teams to assemble standardized functionality without rebuilding it from scratch

Mock Exam 2.q: A security architect is documenting the two-layer security model for a Pega application. She explains the distinction between the step that verifies who a user is and the step that controls what the verified user can do. Authorization in Pega application security primarily determines:
o: The color theme of the portal
The Ruleset version
Who the user is at login
What an authenticated user is allowed to access and do
Mock Exam 2.r: Authorization determines what an already-authenticated user is allowed to do — which Case Types, fields, and actions they can access. It is enforced through Access Roles attached to the user's Access Group, and is always evaluated only after authentication has succeeded

Mock Exam 2.q: A Business Architect is designing the access model for a Claims application. The team discusses how to efficiently configure the same portal and permissions for all junior and senior adjusters without configuring each operator individually. A user is an individual operator; a Persona is:
o: A single Operator record
A landing page
One Access Role only
A category/role of users with shared access needs
Mock Exam 2.r: A Persona represents a role category of users who share the same access needs and UX — for example, 'Claims Adjuster'. Multiple operators can be associated with one Persona, so access rights and portal layouts are configured once for the group rather than per individual

Mock Exam 2.q: Which artifact does the Operator record reference to obtain its application, portals, and roles?
o: A Work Queue
An Access Role directly
An Access Group
A Data Transform
Mock Exam 2.r: Each Operator record points to an Access Group. The Access Group determines the application the operator uses, the portals they can access, their default work group, and the Access Roles — and therefore the permissions — they are granted at runtime

Mock Exam 2.q: Two distinct job functions need different portals and permissions. Best modeling approach?
o: A single Access Role for everyone
One shared Operator record
Rely on authentication alone
Separate Personas, each backed by its own Access Group and Access Roles
Mock Exam 2.r: When two job functions need different portals and permissions, each should be modeled as a distinct Persona. Each Persona is backed by its own Access Group, which references the appropriate Access Roles defining the exact class and action permissions for that role

Mock Exam 2.q: A Lead System Architect is preparing an application for production deployment and reviews the Security Checklist in Dev Studio. A junior developer asks what benefit this tool adds beyond the team's existing secure-coding practices. A key benefit of the Security Checklist is that it:
o: Calculates field values
Automatically routes Assignments
Provides recommended tasks to harden the application and reduce security risk
Generates Insights
Mock Exam 2.r: The Security Checklist in Dev Studio provides a structured list of recommended hardening tasks — such as enabling TLS, removing default accounts, and locking Rulesets — to reduce attack surface before the application goes live. Each item shows a pass or fail status with remediation guidance

Mock Exam 2.q: During a security architecture review, a stakeholder asks the System Architect to clarify how Pega manages permissions across different user groups without setting them per individual. The architect explains the underlying access control model. RBAC stands for and means:
o: Rule-Based Application Configuration
Role-Based Access Control — permissions granted by role
Record-Based Audit Control
Routing By Assignment Category
Mock Exam 2.r: Role-Based Access Control assigns permissions to roles rather than to individuals. In Pega, this is implemented by creating Access Roles that define class and action permissions, then bundling those roles into Access Groups that are assigned to operators by job function

Mock Exam 2.q: A System Architect configures a List View in a portal to display customer records. A business user reports that she cannot edit or delete any records directly from the list. List Views are read-only by default; to allow create, edit, or delete operations, the architect must:
o: Convert it to a Partial View
Enable editing on the List View
Add an Access Role
Change the data source
Mock Exam 2.r: By default, List Views in Pega display data in a read-only format. To allow users to create, edit, or delete records directly from a List View, editing must be explicitly enabled in the view configuration. Without this setting, users can only view the listed data

Mock Exam 2.q: A System Architect is designing portal configuration for a multi-role Claims application. The portal must have different landing pages for customers and agents, and the navigation must reflect their Persona. Which TWO statements correctly describe how Channels and Personas interact in Pega?
o: All Personas within an application must use the same Channel configuration
Each Persona is associated with one or more Channels that define the user interface experience
A user's Channel is selected automatically based on their IP address
A Channel can be configured to show or hide navigation items based on the active Persona
Mock Exam 2.r: Personas are linked to Channels that define the portal experience; Channels can be configured with Persona-specific navigation.

Mock Exam 2.q: Which UI principle does the Pega UI layer subscribe to, connecting front-end components to back-end APIs?
o: Single Source of Truth
Convention over Configuration
Don't Repeat Yourself
Separation of Concerns
Mock Exam 2.r: Pega's UI architecture applies the Separation of Concerns principle to keep front-end components decoupled from back-end APIs and data. Each UI component has a single responsibility, making the layer modular, easier to maintain, and replaceable without affecting the data or process layers

Mock Exam 2.q: On a Case Type's Data Model, which fields are designated as Primary by default?
o: First name and Last name
Label and Description
Create date and Operator
pyGUID and Status
Mock Exam 2.r: When a Case Type is created, Pega automatically marks the Label and Description fields as Primary Fields on the Data Model tab. These two fields appear by default on the Create, Edit, and Details Views without any additional configuration from the architect

Mock Exam 2.q: A System Architect discovers that a flow is taking an unexpected path through a Decision shape. She opens the Tracer and sets a breakpoint. What happens when a Tracer breakpoint is triggered during Case processing?
o: The Case is automatically resolved when the breakpoint fires
The Tracer logs the event and continues processing without interruption
Case processing pauses at that rule execution point, allowing the developer to inspect state before continuing
The breakpoint deletes the event log entry for that rule
Mock Exam 2.r: Setting a breakpoint in the Tracer pauses Case processing at that rule's execution point. The developer can inspect property values and rule state before resuming. This is more than just logging — it actively halts execution, which is why breakpoints are not recommended in production

Mock Exam 2.q: A UX designer asks a System Architect to explain the 'field group' component visible in the View editor. The designer wants to know whether field groups are reusable components that can be placed in multiple Views across the application. A field group in a Pega View is:
o: An Access Role
A cluster of related fields under one header, specific to that View (not reusable)
A reusable rule shared across Views
A Data Page
Mock Exam 2.r: A field group in a View clusters related fields under a shared header, making the form more readable. However, field groups are specific to the View they are defined in — they cannot be reused in other Views. Changes to the group's structure must be made directly within that View

Mock Exam 2.q: A System Architect upgrades a client environment to Pega Infinity '24 and is asked whether GenAI Autopilot features will be immediately available to developers after the upgrade without any additional setup. In Pega Infinity '23 and '24, Pega GenAI Autopilot features are:
o: Removed from the platform
Always on and cannot be disabled
Only available in Dev Studio
Inactive by default and require configuration to enable
Mock Exam 2.r: In Pega Infinity '23 and '24, Pega GenAI Autopilot capabilities are shipped as inactive by default and require explicit configuration to enable. This design gives organizations control over when and how they adopt GenAI features rather than activating them automatically at upgrade

Mock Exam 2.q: A Solutions Consultant uses Pega Blueprint with a client's business stakeholders to rapidly generate an initial application design from a plain-English description of their process. From a business-terms description, Pega Blueprint uses generative AI to propose which of the following?
o: Server hardware and network topology
Only Access Roles
Case Types, Case Life Cycles, Data Models, data objects, and Personas
Only a list of Rulesets
Mock Exam 2.r: Given a business-terms description, Pega Blueprint uses generative AI to propose an initial application structure including Case Types, Case Life Cycles, Data Models, data objects, and Personas. This AI-generated draft is then imported into App Studio for architect review and refinement

Mock Exam 2.q: Which Pega GenAI capability automates Case processing and offers conversational run-time support, governed by Tool Rules?
o: Knowledge Buddy
Pega Blueprint
Pega GenAI Agents
OpenAI search
Mock Exam 2.r: Pega GenAI Agents can run automations — start Cases, invoke other agents, or call external services — and engage in multi-turn conversations with users. Tool Rules govern which automations an Agent can invoke, adding organizational security and auditability to AI-driven processing

Mock Exam 2.q: To develop custom GenAI capabilities using the Pega GenAI gateway, which add-on is used?
o: Pega GenAI Connect
Deployment Manager
Search Assistant
Pega GenAI Coach
Mock Exam 2.r: Pega GenAI Connect is the add-on that exposes the Pega GenAI gateway for building custom generative AI capabilities. It provides the framework for integrating third-party LLMs and creating custom AI-powered Steps and features within Pega applications

Mock Exam 2.q: After configuring a Connect Step's prompt and response mapping, what must you also do so users see the response?
o: Lock the Ruleset
Identify a target field and add it to the application UI
Create an Access Role
Enable unattended RPA
Mock Exam 2.r: You must write the response to a target field and add it to the UI to display it

Mock Exam 2.q: Which TWO are valid response structures for a Pega GenAI Connect Step?
o: Structured - List
Encrypted - Binary
Compiled - Java
Structured - Single
Mock Exam 2.r: A Pega GenAI Connect Step can return one of three response structures: Structured-Single (one object mapped to properties), Structured-List (a list of objects), or Unstructured (raw text mapped to a Text paragraph field). Choosing the correct structure ensures the response is stored in the right field type

Mock Exam 2.q: A DevOps lead is presenting a CI/CD strategy to a new project team and explains the distinction between Continuous Integration, Continuous Delivery, and manual release processes. What does Continuous Delivery primarily accomplish in a Pega DevOps pipeline?
o: Locks developers out of the application
Replaces the Case Life Cycle
Removes the need for environments
Automates releasing validated changes through stages toward production
Mock Exam 2.r: Continuous Delivery automates the process of releasing validated software changes through pipeline stages toward production. By scripting the promotion steps, teams can release more frequently and consistently, reducing manual errors and the risk associated with infrequent, large deployments

Mock Exam 2.q: A GoGoRoad stakeholder requests that the Spanish portal be launched before the full translation package is ready. The SA generates a translation ZIP but notices that picklist values sourced from a Data Page are missing. What must the SA do to include those values?
o: Re-generate the translation package with a different export setting
Manually translate each Data Page source record in Dev Studio
Add the Data Page text via App Studio → Settings → Localization → Additional text
The values are included automatically once the language pack is imported
Mock Exam 2.r: Data Pages are empty at the time of package generation, so their text is not auto-included. The SA must add the specific Data Page-sourced text via App Studio → Settings → Localization → Additional text before generating the final package

Mock Exam 2.q: A Lead System Architect is establishing development guidelines for a team of ten developers working on the same Pega application. She defines standards for how changes should be developed, reviewed, and released to prevent conflicts and unauthorized changes. Which is a recognized release-management best practice in Pega?
o: Never increment versions
Develop in branches and merge when stable/approved; lock older Ruleset versions
Edit production rulesets directly
Skip testing to move faster
Mock Exam 2.r: Release management best practices in Pega include developing in branches so each team member works in isolation, merging only when changes are stable and approved, and locking older Ruleset versions to prevent unauthorized modifications during an active release cycle

Mock Exam 2.q: A manager wants a quick visual of Cases created per day to spot a trend. Which Insight type?
o: A table Insight
A Decision Table
A chart Insight
A BIX extract
Mock Exam 2.r: A chart Insight renders the data query as a bar, line, or pie chart, making it ideal for spotting trends and comparing values over time. Table Insights present row-level detail for drill-down analysis but are less effective for quickly identifying visual patterns or anomalies

Mock Exam 2.q: A System Architect must recommend the right Pega reporting tool for two different teams: operations managers who need daily dashboards within the Pega portal, and a data warehouse team that needs to bulk-extract records for cross-system analytics. Which statement best contrasts Insights and BIX?
o: Both require Dev Studio coding only
They are identical
Insights extract externally; BIX visualizes inside Pega
Insights analyze/visualize data inside Pega; BIX extracts data to external systems
Mock Exam 2.r: Insights create visual reports and saved queries that live inside Pega Platform for operational analysis. BIX (Business Intelligence Exchange) is the complementary tool for bulk-extracting Pega data to external systems, enabling cross-system BI and data warehousing workflows

Mock Exam 2.q: A business manager asks why she should use Pega Insights rather than requesting a custom report from the IT team each time she needs operational data. The architect explains the self-service nature of Insights. A defining benefit of Insights is that they:
o: Must be re-created per user
Require BIX to be viewed
Can be saved and shared between users (self-service, low-code)
Can only be viewed by their creator
Mock Exam 2.r: Insights can be saved and shared between users without writing code, giving business managers self-service access to recurring operational reports. This eliminates the need to request custom reports from IT and ensures all team members are viewing the same consistent analysis

Mock Exam 3.q: A new System Architect is reviewing a Case Life Cycle and notices two colors of Steps: green ones that require operator input and yellow ones that execute automatically without any user interaction. A Step performed by the system — not a user — is called:
o: A Stage
An Automation Step
A Persona
A Collect information Step
Mock Exam 3.r: Steps performed by the system without user interaction are Automation Steps, displayed in yellow in the Case Life Cycle Designer. Steps that require user input are Collect Information Steps, displayed in green. The color coding makes the flow readable at a glance

Mock Exam 3.q: A System Architect is designing a Claims application and needs a Stage to handle rejected or escalated Claims outside the normal approval path. She asks which Case Life Cycle construct is designed for deviations and exceptions. Alternate Stages in a Pega Case Life Cycle are used to:
o: Handle deviations/exceptions from the primary path
Authenticate users
Store data permanently
Always start the Case
Mock Exam 3.r: Alternate Stages sit off the primary Case path and handle exceptions, deviations, or negative outcomes — such as a Rejected or Escalated Stage. The Case is transitioned to an Alternate Stage using a Change Stage Automation shape when a trigger condition is met

Mock Exam 3.q: A System Architect is configuring the Create Stage for a new Case Type. She selects a non-Channel-specific Create Process and notices that only certain Step types are available to add. A non-Channel-specific Create Process can include which Step type only?
o: Automation Steps only
Collect information Steps
Any Step type
Change Stage Steps only
Mock Exam 3.r: A Create Process that is not tied to a specific channel is restricted to Collect Information Steps only. Automation Steps cannot be included because system actions must be deferred until after the Case is fully created and has a unique identifier

Mock Exam 3.q: Which best describes the relationship between a Case Type and a Case?
o: A Case is the model; a Case Type is one instance
A Case Type is one Step in a Case
A Case Type is an abstract repeatable model; a Case is a specific numbered instance
They are identical
Mock Exam 3.r: A Case Type defines the repeatable blueprint — the Stages, Processes, Steps, and data model — that all Cases of that type follow. Each Case is a distinct, numbered runtime instance of its Case Type, representing one specific unit of work being tracked and resolved

Mock Exam 3.q: A System Architect is configuring duplicate Case detection for a health insurance authorization application. She wants to flag Cases as potential duplicates only when the patient date of birth matches exactly, but also score other matching fields. Which TWO statements correctly describe the duplicate detection configuration?
o: All conditions in a duplicate search are weighted and contribute to the total score
Matching secondary fields (name, policy number) should be configured as Weighted conditions that contribute to a score
Date of birth should be configured as a Basic condition — it must match for any duplicate to be flagged
If basic conditions do not match, the Case can still be flagged if weighted score is high enough
Mock Exam 3.r: Basic conditions MUST all match for a Case to be flagged — if date of birth differs, no duplicate is surfaced. Weighted conditions add score to basic-matched candidates.

Mock Exam 3.q: To make a parent Case wait until its child Cases reach a status, use:
o: An SLA deadline
A Decision Table
A case-dependency Wait Step
A timer Wait Step
Mock Exam 3.r: A case-dependency Wait Step causes the parent Case to pause until one or more linked Cases — typically child Cases — reach a specified status, such as Resolved-Completed. Once the condition is met, the parent Case automatically resumes from where it was paused

Mock Exam 3.q: A System Architect is configuring optional Actions on a Claims Case Type. The 'Update Contact Info' action should be available throughout the entire Case lifecycle, but 'Request Reinspection' should only be available during the 'Inspection' Stage. Which TWO statements correctly describe this configuration?
o: Case-wide optional Actions are automatically added to every Stage without configuration
Configure 'Update Contact Info' as a Case-wide optional Action on the Workflow tab
Configure 'Request Reinspection' as a Stage-only optional Action scoped to the 'Inspection' Stage
Both actions must be configured at the Case level — Stage-level optional Actions do not exist
Mock Exam 3.r: Case-wide optional Actions are available throughout the Case lifecycle; Stage-only optional Actions are scoped to a specific Stage. Both are configured on the Workflow tab.

Mock Exam 3.q: A Business Architect is documenting the structure of a Pega application for a new stakeholder. She explains how work is organized from the highest-level phases down to individual units of work. Which ordering correctly describes the Case Life Cycle hierarchy from outermost to innermost?
o: Persona → Stage → Step
Process → Stage → Step
Stage → Process → Step
Step → Process → Stage
Mock Exam 3.r: The Case Life Cycle is organized in three nested levels: Stages are the top-level phases of the lifecycle, Processes group related Steps within a Stage, and Steps are the individual units of work performed by users or the system. This hierarchy structures flow from high-level to granular

Mock Exam 3.q: An overdue Assignment should rise to the top of agents' Worklists automatically. Which mechanism enables this?
o: Increasing Urgency via the SLA goal/deadline
Converting the Step to a Work Queue
Deleting the SLA
Renaming the Ruleset
Mock Exam 3.r: When a Service Level Agreement's goal threshold passes, Pega automatically increases the Assignment's Urgency value. Urgency rises again at the deadline. Higher Urgency moves the Assignment closer to the top of the operator's Worklist, signaling it needs immediate attention

Mock Exam 3.q: Cross-functional work spanning HR, IT, and Facilities on shared queues is organized by:
o: A simulated data source
A When Condition
A single Worklist
A cross-functional Work Group
Mock Exam 3.r: A cross-functional Work Group in Pega associates operators from different departments — such as HR, IT, and Facilities — along with their associated Work Queues under a single group. This enables cross-team collaboration and shared routing of Assignments across organizational boundaries

Mock Exam 3.q: A System Architect is designing a customer onboarding Case Type. The team lead recommends creating a separate child Case for the identity verification step. Which TWO conditions from the following justify using a child Case in this scenario?
o: When a Stage or Process is skipped
Which Steps in a Process execute
Which database server stores the Case
Which operator created the Case
Mock Exam 3.r: When Conditions are the Pega mechanism for conditional logic in the Case Life Cycle. They determine whether a Stage or Process is skipped at runtime and control which individual Steps within a Process execute. Each When Condition evaluates to true or false to drive branching decisions

Mock Exam 3.q: A System Architect is building a Process that automatically generates a background verification sub-Case when a loan application is submitted, without requiring any operator action to trigger it. An Automation shape that creates a related sub-Case without user interaction is:
o: Only valid in the Resolution Stage
Invalid — automations cannot create Cases
Only valid with manual confirmation per field
Valid — Create Case runs without user interaction
