Mock Exam 3.r: Create Case is a standard Automation shape that spins off a linked child Case automatically, without requiring user interaction. Because it executes as a system action, it is a valid Automation shape that can appear anywhere in a Process alongside other system-driven steps

Mock Exam 3.q: A System Architect is designing an approval flow for expense reports under $5,000, which require only one manager's decision. She must decide between a single approval and a cascading approval pattern. A single approval differs from cascading approval in that it:
o: Requires one approver whose outcome routes the Case
Is purely decorative
Never affects the Case path
Requires every user in the org to approve
Mock Exam 3.r: A single approval routes the Assignment to one approver whose decision determines the next path. Cascading approval sends the same work through a sequential chain of approvers — each must act before the next receives it — often organized by an authority matrix

Mock Exam 3.q: A System Architect configures a Wait Step in a parent Case to pause processing until a child 'Vehicle Inspection' Case is resolved. Which TWO conditions must be true for this Wait Step to function correctly?
o: The child Case must be on the same application version as the parent Case
The trigger must be set to one of the two valid statuses: 'To be resolved' or 'Resolved'
The Wait Step must be placed in the Create Stage of the parent Case
A hierarchical parent-child Case relationship must already exist between the two Cases
Mock Exam 3.r: Wait Steps require a hierarchical parent-child relationship and one of two documented trigger statuses ('To be resolved' or 'Resolved').

Mock Exam 3.q: In a Stage with two Processes that must each finish before the Stage advances, but in any order, configure them as:
o: Parallel Processes
Sequential Processes
Optional actions
Alternate Stages
Mock Exam 3.r: Parallel Processes are configured when two or more independent Processes within a Stage can run simultaneously in any order. The Stage does not advance until all parallel Processes complete. Sequential Processes, by contrast, must run one after another in a fixed order

Mock Exam 3.q: Which model focuses on integration settings, local storage, and external systems of record?
o: Conceptual Data Model
Physical Data Model
Logical Data Model
Microjourney model
Mock Exam 3.r: The Physical Data Model captures the implementation-level view of data, including where and how information is stored or retrieved — integration settings, local Pega database tables, and connections to external Systems of Record. It is derived from the Logical Data Model

Mock Exam 3.q: A data object created from the Case Life Cycle designer with no fields or integration is a:
o: Fully configured production object
Draft data object (placeholder)
Savable Data Page
Simulated data source
Mock Exam 3.r: A Draft data object is created when an architect adds a data object from the Case Life Cycle Designer without adding any fields or integration configuration. It is a structural placeholder that must be fully configured with properties and a data source before use in production

Mock Exam 3.q: Within an Order line, a Product sourced from an external DB, one per line, is configured as:
o: Case reference, Single record
Embedded Data, Single record
Data reference, Single record
Data reference, List of records
Mock Exam 3.r: When a product is sourced from an external database rather than entered directly by the user, the relationship type is Data reference, not Embedded Data. Because there is exactly one product per order line, the cardinality is Single record rather than a page list

Mock Exam 3.q: A project manager asks a System Architect to add a 'Status level' field to an existing Customer data object in a running application. The architect explains that this change has broader implications than simply adding a column. From a Pega model-driven perspective, adding a new field to a data object represents:
o: Just a value change with no impact
A Data Page refresh only
A pyGUID reassignment
A change to the object's fields — i.e., a change to the business process
Mock Exam 3.r: Adding a new field to a data object modifies its structure — defining what data the business process captures. In Pega's model-driven approach, changing which fields exist is a process change because it alters what information is collected and tracked during Case processing

Mock Exam 3.q: A System Architect is configuring a Data Page with multiple potential sources — a live REST API and a stub/simulated source for testing. She must determine the correct refresh strategy and sourcing approach. Which TWO statements about Data Page sourcing are correct?
o: The refresh strategy is configured separately from the sourcing and applies to the entire Data Page
Conditional sourcing evaluates sources in order and uses the first one whose condition matches
The last source in the list has no condition and acts as the 'Otherwise' fallback
All sources in a Data Page are queried simultaneously and the fastest response wins
Mock Exam 3.r: Conditional sourcing evaluates sources in configured order; the last source (no condition) is the fallback D correctly describes that the refresh strategy is a separate configuration from sourcing — but since both A and B are the target answers, D is a distractor

Mock Exam 3.q: A System Architect is reviewing the Visual Data Model for a university application where many students can enroll in many courses and each course can have many students. She needs to identify the correct notation for this relationship. Which indicator in the Pega Visual Data Model represents a many-to-many relationship?
o: A circle with multiple lines on both sides
A circle with one line
No icon
A circle with multiple lines on one side
Mock Exam 3.r: In the Pega Visual Data Model, relationship cardinality is encoded by the line style at each end of the connector. Multiple lines on both sides represent a many-to-many relationship; a single line on one side indicates one-to-many; single lines on both sides indicate one-to-one

Mock Exam 3.q: A System Architect is configuring a savable Data Page to update a customer's contact information in an external CRM using a REST connector. Which TWO statements about the save plan configuration are correct?
o: When Conditions on save targets are optional and have no effect on which SOR receives the data
When Conditions on individual save targets allow committing to multiple data tables conditionally
The Connector save option also supports SOAP-based web service calls for external saves
The Connector save option in the save plan supports REST-based saves to external systems only (not SOAP)
Mock Exam 3.r: The Connector save option is REST-only — not SOAP. When Conditions on save targets enable conditional routing to multiple tables or systems.

Mock Exam 3.q: A System Architect is configuring a Total Price field on an Order Case Type that must automatically equal the sum of all line item prices and update whenever any price changes. Which statement about how a calculated field works in Pega Platform is correct?
o: It is computed from a formula over other fields and recalculates as inputs change
It is a free-text field users fill
It stores the system of record
It defines user authorization
Mock Exam 3.r: A calculated field derives its value from a formula applied to other fields in the Case and automatically recalculates whenever its inputs change. Because its value is determined by logic rather than user input, calculated fields are typically set to read-only in the View

Mock Exam 3.q: A data object is reusable across an application's Case Types primarily to:
o: Save development effort and ensure data consistency
Avoid using fields
Force each Case Type to use different data
Prevent reuse
Mock Exam 3.r: Making a data object reusable means it can be referenced from multiple Case Types in the same application. This avoids duplicating field definitions, reduces maintenance effort when the structure changes, and ensures the same data — such as Customer or Address — behaves consistently everywhere

Mock Exam 3.q: A System Architect is explaining Decision Table evaluation to a Business Architect who is configuring shipping tier logic. The BA wants to understand what happens when the input values match more than one row in the table. Which statement about Decision Table evaluation behavior is correct?
o: All matching rows are averaged
A random matching row returns
Rows evaluate top-to-bottom; the first matching row's result is returned
The last row always returns
Mock Exam 3.r: A Decision Table evaluates rows from top to bottom and returns the result of the first row whose conditions all match the input values. Evaluation stops immediately — no further rows are checked. If no row matches, the 'otherwise' default result is returned

Mock Exam 3.q: A SA needs to initialize fields in a new Case by copying the customer's address from a form submission and converting a date string to a Date field. Which TWO of the following are valid uses of a Data Transform?
o: Set/initialize field values to keep Views consistent
Copy data from one page/Case to another
Authenticate a user at login
Define which portal a user sees
Mock Exam 3.r: Data Transforms are rules that set, copy, or transform property values — for example, copying an applicant's address into a Case or converting a date string to a typed Date field. They operate on data properties only and are not involved in authentication, portal layouts, or access control

Mock Exam 3.q: A System Architect is configuring a Pega application that writes customer updates to an external CRM via a Savable Data Page. The team is concerned about data consistency if the CRM becomes temporarily unavailable. During an external CRM outage, a properly configured Savable Data Page helps by:
o: Routing to a Work Queue
Managing the transaction so systems stay synchronized even if an error occurs
Deleting the Case
Disabling validation
Mock Exam 3.r: A Savable Data Page uses a configured data save plan to write data back to a System of Record. A well-designed save plan can include transactional rollback or retry logic, helping keep the Pega Case and the external system synchronized even when an integration error occurs

Mock Exam 3.q: A Lead System Architect is presenting Pega application design principles to a client planning an enterprise rollout across multiple business units. She explains how shared components can be packaged for reuse rather than rebuilt in each application. Which of the following best describes modular enterprise reuse in Pega?
o: Configuring servers via CLI
Assembling standardized, pre-tested components instead of building from scratch
Writing all logic in Java
Outsourcing all development
Mock Exam 3.r: Modular enterprise reuse is the practice of building standardized, pre-tested components once — such as an authentication module or a document-generation service — and assembling them into multiple applications. This accelerates delivery and ensures consistent behavior across every application that includes the module

Mock Exam 3.q: A Lead SA is onboarding new System Architects to a project. She explains that Pega supports two types of inheritance. Which TWO statements correctly describe the difference between pattern inheritance and directed inheritance?
o: Pattern inheritance is automatic and based on shared class-name prefixes
Directed inheritance explicitly names the parent class on the class form, enabling inheritance from outside the business hierarchy
Both pattern and directed inheritance require explicit configuration on the class form
Directed inheritance is used to inherit from Pega's built-in Work- and Data- classes
Mock Exam 3.r: Pattern inheritance is automatic (prefix-based); directed inheritance is explicit (configured on the class form) D describes a valid use case for directed inheritance, but since 'used to' implies exclusivity, it's a distractor here

Mock Exam 3.q: A System Architect is explaining to a new team member why Pega organizes rules into different classes — such as Work, Integration, and Data classes — rather than using a flat structure. The new member asks what principle determines which class a given rule belongs to. Rules are grouped into classes according to their:
o: Capacity for reuse
Creation date
Color
Operator
Mock Exam 3.r: In Pega, rules are organized into classes based on their reuse scope. Work classes hold rules for processing Cases, Integration classes contain connector rules for external systems, and Data classes define data types and properties. Grouping by reuse capacity enables efficient rule resolution and inheritance

Mock Exam 3.q: A System Architect is explaining Pega's class hierarchy and Pattern inheritance to a new developer. She uses the class name TGB-IT-Work as an example to illustrate how inheritance relationships are encoded directly in class names. In the class TGB-IT-Work, which statement about the inheritance hierarchy is correct?
o: TGB-IT-Work is a child of TGB-IT, which is a child of TGB
TGB is the most specific class
The hyphens carry no meaning
TGB-IT-Work is the parent of TGB
Mock Exam 3.r: In the class name TGB-IT-Work, each hyphen-separated segment encodes a level of the class hierarchy: TGB-IT-Work inherits from TGB-IT, which inherits from TGB. Rule resolution searches the most-specific class first, then walks up the hierarchy until a matching rule is found

Mock Exam 3.q: A System Architect notices a pattern of nearly identical Flow rules in a Pega application — one for each product type — with the only difference being a hard-coded value. She recommends a refactoring approach to reduce this duplication. To increase a rule's reusability and avoid many near-duplicate versions, the best practice is to use:
o: Moving the rule to the Integration class
Parametrization (drive logic by a passed parameter)
Adding more patch versions
Locking all Rulesets
Mock Exam 3.r: Parametrization makes a rule reusable by accepting an input parameter that varies the logic at runtime. Instead of creating near-duplicate rules for each variation, one parameterized rule handles all cases by switching on the passed value, significantly reducing the Ruleset's footprint

Mock Exam 3.q: A System Architect needs to make an advanced SLA rule built in Dev Studio available to App Studio developers so they can select it from the SLA drop-down. Which TWO steps are required?
o: Mark the SLA rule as a relevant record in Dev Studio using Actions → Mark as relevant record
Verify the rule is guardrail-compliant before marking it — violations block promotion
Mark the SLA rule as a relevant record in App Studio using the Case Designer toolbar
Add the SLA rule to the Ruleset stack in the application settings
Mock Exam 3.r: Marking a rule as a relevant record in Dev Studio (via Actions menu) makes it visible in App Studio drop-downs. Guardrail compliance must be verified first.

Mock Exam 3.q: A standalone, comprehensive Pega application for managing backlogs, sprints, and teams is:
o: Prediction Studio
Agile Workbench
Admin Studio
Agile Studio
Mock Exam 3.r: Agile Studio is a standalone, full-featured Pega application for managing backlogs, sprints, releases, and teams at scale. Agile Workbench is the lightweight counterpart — embedded directly in App Studio for capturing quick user stories and feedback alongside the Case Designer

Mock Exam 3.q: A System Architect is reviewing accessibility requirements for a new Constellation-based Pega application. Which TWO accessibility standards does Pega's Constellation architecture comply with by default?
o: PCI DSS Payment Card security standard
ISO 9001 Quality Management
WCAG 2.1 (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines)
Section 508 of the US Rehabilitation Act
Mock Exam 3.r: Pega Constellation is built with WCAG 2.1 and Section 508 compliance embedded in its core patterns. These standards apply to web content accessibility and US federal accessibility requirements respectively. ISO 9001 and PCI DSS address quality management and payment security — unrelated to accessibility

Mock Exam 3.q: A System Architect is onboarding a new team member experienced in App Studio who must now work in Dev Studio. He asks about the Dev Studio equivalents for common App Studio terms like 'User', 'Field', and 'Team'. Which of the following is the correct App Studio → Dev Studio naming mapping?
o: Field → Class
Goal and deadline → Property
Team → Ruleset
User → Operator
Mock Exam 3.r: Pega uses different terminology between App Studio and Dev Studio. In App Studio 'User' maps to 'Operator' in Dev Studio, 'Field' maps to 'Property', 'Goal and deadline' maps to 'SLA', and 'Team' maps to 'Work Group'. The underlying platform artifacts are identical in both studios

Mock Exam 3.q: A System Architect is reviewing the security architecture of a Pega application with a client's security team. The client asks about the correct order of the two fundamental security steps that occur when a user logs in to the application. Which sequence correctly describes the two security steps at login?
o: Authorize first, then authenticate
Authenticate first (identity), then authorize (permissions)
Both only after the Case resolves
Neither if a Persona exists
Mock Exam 3.r: Authentication must always precede authorization. First, the system verifies who the user is through credentials, tokens, or MFA. Once identity is confirmed, authorization evaluates the user's Access Roles to determine which applications, Case Types, and actions they are permitted to use

Mock Exam 3.q: A manager needs extra permission to approve high-value Cases. Where is this best changed?
o: A default value on a field
The manager Persona's Access Group/Access Roles
The authentication provider
A Wait Step
Mock Exam 3.r: To grant a manager additional permissions, the correct place to update is the Access Roles referenced within their Access Group, which is tied to their Persona. Access Roles define the class-level and action-level permissions; the Access Group bundles them with the application and portals

Mock Exam 3.q: A claims manager notices that some operators can see the 'Approve' button on a Case while others cannot, even when viewing the same Case Type. The System Architect explains which security artifact controls this difference. Which artifact in Pega RBAC determines which work assignments and functionality a user can access?
o: Their Persona/Access Group and the Access Roles it grants
The number of Cases
The portal color theme
The Ruleset version
Mock Exam 3.r: What a user can access and action in Pega is entirely governed by RBAC: the user's Persona determines their Access Group, and the Access Group references the Access Roles that grant specific class and action permissions. Changing any of these three artifacts changes what the user sees and can do

Mock Exam 3.q: A Lead System Architect is designing the security model for a new Pega application. She explains to a junior developer the difference between an Access Role and an Access Group, clarifying which artifact defines what a user is permitted to do. An Access Role in Pega RBAC primarily:
o: Caches data in memory
Bundles the application and portals
Defines permissions (what classes/actions a user may use)
Stores the user's credentials
Mock Exam 3.r: An Access Role specifies which classes and actions a user is permitted to use — it is the core permission artifact in Pega's RBAC model. Access Groups bundle one or more Access Roles with an application, portal layouts, and a default work group to form the complete operator profile

Mock Exam 3.q: During a security training session, a System Architect asks a group of developers to identify what specific question the authentication step answers when a user logs in to a Pega application, distinguishing it from the authorization step. Authentication in a Pega application primarily answers which question?
o: Which portal do you see?
How urgent is the work?
What are you allowed to do?
Are you really who you say you are?
Mock Exam 3.r: Authentication answers 'Are you who you say you are?' by verifying credentials, tokens, or MFA codes. Authorization is a separate subsequent step that answers 'What are you allowed to do?' by evaluating the user's Access Roles and class-level permissions within the application

Mock Exam 3.q: A project manager questions whether running the Security Checklist is necessary since the development team already follows secure coding practices. A System Architect explains the additional value the checklist provides beyond normal code review. Why should a System Architect use the Security Checklist before go-live?
o: To systematically harden the app and reduce security risk
To create Personas
To replace SLAs
To increase the number of Cases
Mock Exam 3.r: The Security Checklist in Pega Dev Studio presents a structured list of recommended security hardening tasks — such as enabling TLS, disabling default accounts, and locking production Rulesets — and marks each as pass or fail, giving teams a systematic approach to reducing vulnerabilities before go-live

Mock Exam 3.q: A loan officer must read submitted data but not change it, while entering an approve/reject decision. Best View design?
o: Make all fields editable
Hide the customer data entirely
Use a List View with bulk actions
Display customer data read-only; provide editable decision fields
Mock Exam 3.r: This View design uses per-field editability: the customer's submitted data is shown in read-only display fields so the officer cannot accidentally alter it, while the approve/reject decision and supporting notes use editable fields. Pega's View configuration supports this mixed-editability layout natively

Mock Exam 3.q: A System Architect is configuring a Constellation portal theme for a banking application. She needs to apply the corporate brand colors without modifying the built-in Pegasus theme. Which TWO statements correctly describe the correct approach?
o: Directly edit the built-in Pegasus theme to add brand colors
Custom themes default to 'Private' visibility when first created
Place shared design system configurations (themes, fonts, icons) in the Enterprise/COE layer for reuse
Copy the built-in theme to create a custom theme, then apply branding changes to the copy
Mock Exam 3.r: Built-in themes cannot be directly edited — they must be copied first. The Enterprise/COE layer is the correct place for shared design configurations so all applications inherit them.

Mock Exam 3.q: A new requirement adds an Account number field. Best practice is to:
o: Build the Data Model first in the Data tab (reuse + inheritance), though you can add from a View
Always add fields from Views; never use the Data tab
Add fields only in Dev Studio
Avoid adding the field
Mock Exam 3.r: The recommended practice is to define new fields on the Case Type's Data Model tab first, which ensures proper class inheritance and reuse across all Views. While Pega also allows adding a field directly from within a View, doing so bypasses the Data Model and makes the field harder to share

Mock Exam 3.q: A reference field to a data object causes which fields to inherit into the Case Type's Views automatically?
o: The referenced object's Primary Fields
All of the object's fields
Only Label and Description
None
Mock Exam 3.r: When a data reference field is added to a Case Type, Pega automatically makes the Primary Fields of the referenced data object available as inherited properties in the Case Type's Views. This means the referenced object's most important fields appear in the Case without additional field-by-field mapping

Mock Exam 3.q: A System Architect notices that property values in a Case are incorrect after a Data Transform runs. She needs to see the exact sequence of rule executions and which properties changed and to what values. Which Pega debugging tool provides this information?
o: The UI Inspector, which surfaces component structure and CSS but not rule execution order
The Clipboard viewer, which shows current page structure but not execution history
The Tracer, which logs each rule executed and highlights property changes in yellow
The Xray tool, which reveals field security and page structure but does not trace flows
Mock Exam 3.r: The Tracer is the dedicated runtime debugging tool. It shows every rule that fires, property changes (highlighted yellow), and the execution path. The other tools (Clipboard, UI Inspector, Xray) are for data state, UI structure, and field security respectively — not flow tracing

Mock Exam 3.q: A System Architect is configuring Steps in the Workflow tab and notices Pega automatically assigns the Default form template to each Step's View. She explains to a junior developer when this auto-assignment does NOT apply. The Default Form template is assigned automatically unless the architect:
o: Add an Access Role
Create a different View type on the UX tab
Delete the Ruleset
Increase the SLA goal
Mock Exam 3.r: Form Views default to the Default form template; other templates come from other View types on the UX tab

Mock Exam 3.q: Which Pega GenAI tools operate at DESIGN time to help build an application?
o: Pega Blueprint and Pega GenAI Autopilot
Pega GenAI Coach and Agents
OpenAI search only
Knowledge Buddy and Search Assistant
Mock Exam 3.r: Pega GenAI Blueprint and Autopilot both operate during application design: Blueprint proposes the initial structure before build begins, while Autopilot accelerates configuration inside App Studio. Pega GenAI Coach and Agents operate at runtime, assisting operators and automating Case processing

Mock Exam 3.q: A client's IT manager is evaluating a Pega Platform upgrade to access GenAI capabilities such as Blueprint, Autopilot, Coach, and Knowledge Buddy. The System Architect must specify the minimum platform release required. Beginning with which Pega Infinity release did the Pega GenAI suite become available?
o: Pega Infinity '23
Pega Platform 8.4
Pega Infinity '25 only
Pega Infinity '21
Mock Exam 3.r: The Pega GenAI product suite — including Blueprint, Autopilot, Coach, Knowledge Buddy, and Agents — was first introduced in the Pega Infinity '23 release. Organizations running earlier versions of Pega Platform must upgrade to access any of these generative AI capabilities

Mock Exam 3.q: A business stakeholder asks whether adopting Pega Blueprint means the team will no longer need to use App Studio for application development. The System Architect clarifies the relationship between the two tools. Pega Blueprint augments which Pega tool rather than replacing it?
o: Pearson VUE
Admin Studio
Prediction Studio
App Studio
Mock Exam 3.r: Pega Blueprint is designed to complement App Studio, not replace it. Blueprint generates an initial application design using generative AI; that design is imported into App Studio where architects refine and implement it. The full build still happens in the Pega studios after Blueprint

Mock Exam 3.q: A System Architect is demonstrating Pega GenAI Autopilot to a QA lead who wants to reduce the time the team spends manually creating test data each sprint. The architect highlights a specific Autopilot feature that directly addresses this testing bottleneck. Which Pega GenAI Autopilot capability eases testing effort?
o: Generate sample records and auto-fill a running Case's form with sample data
Mark rules as relevant records
Lock the topmost Ruleset
Provision a production database
Mock Exam 3.r: Pega GenAI Autopilot includes a testing-assistance capability that generates realistic sample data records and auto-fills an open Case's form fields during test runs. This reduces the manual effort of creating test data and lets architects quickly verify that forms and flows behave as designed

Mock Exam 3.q: A System Architect is presenting Pega GenAI features to an insurance client whose employees frequently need to look up internal policy rules during Case processing. The client asks which feature would let employees ask natural-language questions and get immediate answers without leaving Pega. Knowledge Buddy provides value by:
o: Compiling Java
Giving instant, contextual answers from the org's procedural docs and knowledge bases
Deploying applications
Routing Assignments
Mock Exam 3.r: Pega Knowledge Buddy answers natural-language questions by searching the organization's own procedural documents, policies, and knowledge bases. It provides client-specific, contextual answers within the Pega application, giving users instant guidance without switching to external search tools

Mock Exam 3.q: A System Architect is importing a Pega Blueprint design into an existing Pega application. A junior developer asks what happens to the assets generated during the import — specifically where they are placed and whether any exceptions apply. Which TWO statements about Pega Blueprint import are correct?
o: Only the BA can import a Blueprint
Import always overwrites the production database
A Blueprint can be imported into a new OR an existing application
All imported assets are placed in a Branch except Access Roles
Mock Exam 3.r: A Blueprint can be imported into either a new or an existing Pega application. All imported assets — Case Types, Data Models, Personas — are placed into a Branch for review before merging. Access Roles are the exception: they are not placed in a Branch and require a Lead System Architect to configure them

Mock Exam 3.q: A DevOps lead is evaluating Pega tools to automate the promotion of application changes from development through QA and staging to production without custom scripting. He asks the System Architect which Pega tool provides a built-in model-driven CI/CD pipeline. Which Pega tool provides a model-driven CI/CD pipeline?
o: Pega Robot Manager
Pega Deployment Manager
Agile Workbench
Prediction Studio
Mock Exam 3.r: Pega Deployment Manager provides a model-driven CI/CD pipeline that automates the promotion of application changes through environments — from development through QA, staging, and into production. Built-in quality gates, such as test runs and guardrail checks, enforce standards at each stage before promotion proceeds

Mock Exam 3.q: A System Architect has completed building a Pega application for a French-speaking audience. She generates a translation package but finds that step instruction text (stored in Paragraph Rules) is missing from the ZIP file. How should she localize this content?
o: Add the Paragraph Rules to the Additional text section in App Studio Localization settings
The Paragraph Rules will be auto-translated when the language pack is imported

Edit the

tags in the paragraph/translated folder files within the ZIP, then re-import
Re-generate the ZIP with the Include Paragraph Rules option checked
Mock Exam 3.r:
Step instructions in Paragraph Rules are NOT auto-extracted into the translation package. To localize them, the SA must manually edit the

tags in the paragraph/translated folder within the ZIP file, then re-upload and import the compressed folder

Mock Exam 3.q: A QA lead is designing an automated testing strategy for a Pega application release. She asks the System Architect which two categories of tests are most important to include in the CI/CD pipeline before promoting changes to production. Which TWO test types help ensure successful deployment?
o: Automated unit tests
Manual re-typing of all data
Scenario (end-to-end) tests
Deleting the staging environment
Mock Exam 3.r: Automated unit tests verify individual rules and logic in isolation to catch defects early in the pipeline. Scenario tests (end-to-end) validate complete workflow paths through the application. Running both types ensures that changes work at the unit level and integrate correctly before reaching production

Mock Exam 3.q: A business analyst asks the System Architect what display formats are available when she saves a data query as an Insight in Pega Platform. She wants to find a format that works for both detailed row-level data review and visual trend analysis. An Insight can be rendered as which of the following output formats?
o: An Access Group or Ruleset
A Wait Step or SLA
A table or a chart/visualization
A Branch or Workspace
Mock Exam 3.r: An Insight in Pega Platform renders a saved data query as either a structured table — for row-level drill-down — or as a chart such as a bar, line, or pie graph for visual trend analysis. The same underlying query can be toggled between these output formats depending on the intended audience

Mock Exam 3.q: A System Architect is advising a client on Pega reporting options. The data warehouse team needs to pull millions of Pega Case records nightly into an external analytics platform, while the operations team needs daily dashboards inside the Pega portal. Which scenario is the clearest fit for BIX rather than Insights?
o: A shareable table inside App Studio
Large-scale extraction of Pega data into an external data warehouse for cross-system BI
A quick in-app bar chart of Cases by status
Exploring data on the Explore Data landing page
Mock Exam 3.r: BIX (Business Intelligence Exchange) is designed for large-scale extraction of Pega application data into external data warehouses or BI platforms. Insights, by contrast, create visualizations and saved queries that remain within the Pega application for operational monitoring and self-service reporting

Mock Exam 3.q: A business operations manager asks the System Architect to explain the business value of building Pega Insights before her team invests time learning to create them. The architect explains what operational problem Insights solve. Why do organizations use Insights in Pega Platform?
o: To define Access Roles
To analyze operations and understand team and process performance for better decisions
To authenticate operators
To route Assignments
Mock Exam 3.r: Organizations use Insights to monitor key operational metrics — such as open Cases by region, average resolution time, or assignment backlog — directly within Pega Platform. This visibility helps managers and teams identify bottlenecks, track performance, and make data-driven process improvements

Mock Exam 4.q: A customer service representative opens a refund request case, determines it is a duplicate, and resolves it. The case status changes to Resolved-Duplicate. What happens to the case next?
o: The duplicate cases are automatically merged into one case.
The case is routed to the manager for resolution.
The duplicate case is moved to a queue to be merged later.
Processing of the case terminates.
Mock Exam 4.r: When a case is resolved with a Resolved-Duplicate status, it is closed and no further processing occurs. The case is not automatically merged or routed; it simply terminates, freeing up the operator's worklist

Mock Exam 4.q: On a service level, the passed deadline interval is measured from __________.
o: The end of the deadline interval.
When the assignment is ready for a user.
When a user begins the assignment.
The end of the goal interval.
Mock Exam 4.r: The Passed Deadline interval starts counting only after the Deadline interval has fully elapsed. It is used to trigger escalating actions (e.g., repeated email reminders) at regular intervals beyond the deadline

Mock Exam 4.q: You are designing a case type that includes a process to perform when a case is rejected. How do you model this requirement in the case life cycle?
o: Add the rejection process to all the primary stages as an optional process.
Add an alternate stage and add the rejection process to the stage.
Add a primary stage and add the rejection process to the stage.
Add an alternate stage and add the rejection process as an optional process to the stage.
Mock Exam 4.r: Rejection is a deviation from the standard lifecycle and belongs in an Alternate Stage. The rejection process is added directly to that alternate stage, not as an optional process, so it runs when the case transitions to that stage

Mock Exam 4.q: Which requirement is satisfied by configuring a service level agreement?
o: Users are notified when they receive an assignment.
Requests from customers with elite status go to a dedicated work group.
A transaction review is completed within 24 hours.
Transaction dispute cases are considered more urgent than address change cases.
Mock Exam 4.r: SLAs define time-based goals and deadlines for completing assignments or cases. Configuring an SLA on a step ensures the assignment must be completed within the specified time, triggering escalations if the goal or deadline is missed

Mock Exam 4.q: A new hire process includes a Screen Job Applicant assignment. The recruiter should complete it within 24 hours. If not completed, the system automatically sends an email to the hiring manager. How do you configure this process?
o: Add a notification to the assignment.
Add a Send Email shape to the process after the assignment.
Add a SendCorrespondence flow action to the assignment.
Add an SLA with an escalation action to the assignment.
Mock Exam 4.r: SLAs support escalation actions triggered when the goal or deadline passes. Adding an SLA with an escalation action to the assignment enables the automated email notification to the hiring manager when the 24-hour goal is exceeded

Mock Exam 4.q: An insurance claim case type has a Review Claim step configured to set the status to Pending-Investigation. When is this status set?
o: When the Process claim stage starts.
When the Review claim step starts.
When the Investigate claim step completes.
When the Review claim step completes.
Mock Exam 4.r: Case status set on a step is applied when that step begins, not when it completes. This allows the status to reflect what the case is currently undergoing, giving operators and managers real-time visibility into the case state

Mock Exam 4.q: An assignment can be routed to which of the following? (Choose two)
o: An access group.
A work queue (work basket).
Multiple operators simultaneously.
A single operator.
Mock Exam 4.r: Assignments in Pega can be routed to a specific operator's Worklist (push routing) or to a Work Queue (work basket) where any qualified operator can pick it up (pull routing). Routing to multiple operators simultaneously or an access group directly is not a standard routing option

Mock Exam 4.q: In a purchase application, customers create purchase requests containing line items. If a product is not in stock, the application creates a purchase order processed by the purchasing team. Which two entities would you model as case types? (Choose two)
o: Customer.
Line item.
Purchase order.
Purchase request.
Mock Exam 4.r: Case types model entities that have their own lifecycle with stages, steps, and assignments. Purchase Request and Purchase Order each have distinct workflows. Customers and Line Items are data objects without independent lifecycles and should be modeled as Data Types

Mock Exam 4.q: An applicant submits a loan request. After credit validation, if acceptable, a loan officer reviews. If approved, it goes to underwriting; if rejected, the customer is notified. Which case life cycle design most closely follows stage naming guidelines?
o: Primary: New→Review→Rejected→Underwriting.
Primary: New→Credit Check→Review→Underwriting; Alternate: Rejected.
Primary: Loan Submitted→Check Credit→Review Loan→Fund Loan; Alternate: Reject Request.
Primary: Loan Request→Loan Reviewed→Loan Rejected→Loan Funded.
Mock Exam 4.r: Best practice for stage naming uses short, action-oriented noun phrases that describe the business state. Primary stages should represent the normal path (New, Credit Check, Review, Underwriting) and resolution paths like Rejected belong in alternate stages

Mock Exam 4.q: What is the recommended number of steps per stage following the best practice for case decomposition?
o: Less than 15.
Mock Exam 4.r: Pega best practice recommends 7 ±2 steps per stage, based on Miller's Law (cognitive load). Keeping steps within this range ensures manageability and clarity for both developers and business stakeholders reviewing the case life cycle

Mock Exam 4.q: During a playback, you place a flow in draft mode to address which limitation?
o: To prevent additional shapes from being added to the flow.
To avoid errors due to references to rules that do not yet exist.
To allow users to choose decision outcomes if a decision rule is not yet available.
To save an incomplete flow.
Mock Exam 4.r: Draft mode allows a flow to run even when it references rules that have not yet been created. This is useful during early development playbacks where the full rule set does not exist yet but the process flow needs to be demonstrated

Mock Exam 4.q: Each row of a Decision Table consists of one or more testable conditions. How does Pega Platform determine when to return the specified result for a row?
o: When the first condition in the row is true.
When all the conditions in the row are true.
When any one of the conditions in the row is true.
When the last condition in the row is true.
Mock Exam 4.r: In a Decision Table, Pega evaluates all conditions in a row as a logical AND. Only when every condition in the row evaluates to true does Pega return that row's result. Rows are evaluated top to bottom until a match is found

Mock Exam 4.q: An insurance company employs appraisers qualified for either art or wine collection appraisals only. How do you configure the router so assignments go to a qualified appraiser?
o: Associate each appraiser to a work group that uses work group parameters.
Associate each appraiser to a work group that uses skill parameters.
Associate each appraiser to one of two work groups corresponding to the appraisal qualifications.
Associate each appraiser to the general appraiser work group.
Mock Exam 4.r: Skill-based routing uses skill parameters on the work group to match assignments to operators with the right qualifications. A single work group with skill parameters is more flexible than creating separate work groups per specialty

Mock Exam 4.q: What is the most flexible sub-case creation method?
o: Procedurally.
Conditionally.
Automatically.
Manually.
Mock Exam 4.r: Manual sub-case creation gives the operator full control over when to create a child case and how many to create. It is the most flexible option, though automatic (always creates) and conditional (based on data) creation cover most automated needs

Mock Exam 4.q: Which requirement would be implemented through circumstancing?
o: An application sends a notification to a manager if a request requires approval; otherwise notifies the employee.
An application sends an email confirming account opening; for customers in certain states, the email includes a mandatory disclosure.
An application sends a text if a customer provides a mobile number, otherwise sends an email.
An application computes shipping; if order exceeds $100, the customer gets a 50% credit.
Mock Exam 4.r: Circumstancing allows the same rule to behave differently based on a property value (like state/region) without copying the rule. Adding a mandatory disclosure for certain states is a classic circumstancing use case—the base email rule is specialized for the state condition

Mock Exam 4.q: What is the best way to cache data from an external system?
o: Data Page.
Report Definition.
Data Table.
Data Transform.
Mock Exam 4.r: Data Pages are purpose-built for caching external data. They load once on first access, can be scoped to Thread, Requestor, or Node levels, and support configurable refresh strategies (e.g., Reload if older than X minutes), making them ideal for caching external system data

Mock Exam 4.q: Your online shopping application serves international customers. You need a data page holding currency exchange rates accessible to all users on the server. What scope should be set?
o: Thread.
Node.
Application.
Requestor.
Mock Exam 4.r: Node scope shares the data page across all requestors on the same server node, avoiding redundant external calls. This is ideal for relatively static shared data like currency exchange rates. Requestor scope would create a separate page per user; Thread scope per thread

Mock Exam 4.q: A data page holds local weather information with 'Reload if Older Than' set to 10 minutes. Created at 11:22. User refreshes at 11:28, then at 11:40. When is the data page reloaded?
Mock Exam 4.r: 'Reload if older than 10 minutes' means the page is reloaded only when it is accessed AND it was last loaded more than 10 minutes ago. At 11:28 (6 min old), no reload. At 11:40 (18 min old), the page is reloaded on access

Mock Exam 4.q: When are data pages created?
o: When a case is created.
All of the above.
When an assignment starts.
When first accessed.
Mock Exam 4.r: Data pages are created lazily—only when first accessed. This on-demand approach avoids loading unnecessary data and is a key performance optimization. The data page is then cached per its configured scope (Thread, Requestor, or Node) for subsequent accesses

Mock Exam 4.q: In which two situations do you use a Data Transform? (Choose two)
o: Create properties after creating a case.
Copy data from one page to another.
Set a default property value.
Reuse properties in two forms.
Mock Exam 4.r: Data Transforms are used to copy data between clipboard pages and to initialize or set property values. They are the preferred, guardrail-compliant alternative to Activities for these operations in Pega 8 and later

Mock Exam 4.q: For which reason do you use a Declare Expression to calculate values in a travel reservation process?
o: To perform the calculation when a form is submitted.
To perform the calculation when the user clicks a button.
To perform the calculation wherever a field is updated.
To perform the calculation in a specific case stage.
Mock Exam 4.r: Declare Expressions use forward chaining by default—they recalculate automatically whenever any source property changes, regardless of where in the application the change occurs. This makes them ideal for real-time calculations like running totals

Mock Exam 4.q: You have forms for a vacation booking process. Declare Expressions calculate flight, hotel, car rental, and tax costs. The last form shows the total credit card charge. How do you configure the total to calculate only when the user reaches the last form?
o: Use backward chaining for all expressions.
Use backward chaining for the total amount expression; forward chaining for all other expressions.
Use forward chaining for all expressions.
Use forward chaining for the total amount expression; backward chaining for all other expressions.
Mock Exam 4.r: Backward chaining calculates a value only when it is accessed or needed. Using backward chaining on the grand total means it is computed only when the last form (which displays it) is reached, avoiding unnecessary computation on earlier forms

Mock Exam 4.q: In an application, three email addresses (work, home, and other) can be captured for a customer. You use .Email(work) to refer to the work email. What type of property is used?
o: Value list.
Page.
Value group.
Page group.
Mock Exam 4.r: A Value Group stores multiple single values indexed by a key (e.g., work, home, other). The parenthetical notation .Email(work) is characteristic of a Value Group. A Value List uses numeric indices, while Page Group and Page store embedded page structures

Mock Exam 4.q: How would you model a one-to-many relationship (e.g., one customer with multiple addresses)?
o: Page group.
Page list.
Page.
Value group.
Mock Exam 4.r: A Page List stores an ordered collection of embedded pages, making it ideal for one-to-many relationships like a customer with multiple addresses. Each entry in the list is a full page with its own set of properties (street, city, zip, etc.)

Mock Exam 4.q: You are developing a purchase application integrating with an external inventory system. A __________ allows Pega to request information from the inventory management system.
o: Service.
Connector.
Report Definition.
Data page.
Mock Exam 4.r: A Connector is an outbound integration mechanism that allows Pega to call an external system and retrieve data. Services are inbound (external systems call Pega). Data pages use connectors internally to fetch and cache external data

Mock Exam 4.q: A purchase request case is created from an inbound email. The application also fetches currency rates from an external system. What should you use for each integration?
o: Service for case creation; connector for currency.
Service for both integrations.
Connector for case creation; service for currency.
Connector for both integrations.
Mock Exam 4.r: Services handle inbound calls—external systems calling Pega (email→case). Connectors handle outbound calls—Pega calling external systems (fetching currency rates). Using the correct direction-appropriate integration component is a Pega best practice

Mock Exam 4.q: In which situation would you use a SQL connector?
o: Write to a table as part of a distributed transaction.
Execute a complex SQL statement such as a stored procedure.
Retrieve a large list of reference data.
Update a table in an external database.
Mock Exam 4.r: SQL connectors are specifically designed for executing complex SQL operations like stored procedures that cannot be expressed through standard Pega data access mechanisms. For simple reads/writes, Report Definitions or Data Pages with standard connectors are preferred

Mock Exam 4.q: What does an Access Group NOT store?
o: Primary portal.
How users are authenticated.
List of roles assigned.
Application record.
Mock Exam 4.r: Authentication method is configured at the authentication service or operator level, not in the Access Group. Access Groups store: the associated application, the primary portal, available portals, and the access roles (privilege sets) assigned to group members

Mock Exam 4.q: What is the primary use of a Ruleset?
o: Manage rule versions.
Configure applications.
Group rules together.
Easy deployment and migration.
Mock Exam 4.r: The primary purpose of a Ruleset is to group related rules together for management and reuse. Rulesets also facilitate versioning and migration as secondary benefits, but grouping rules by application layer or functional area is their fundamental role

Mock Exam 4.q: Which is a strictly one-to-one mapping in Pega?
o: Operator ID → Access group.
Access group → Portal.
Access group → Application.
Operator ID → Portal.
Mock Exam 4.r: Each Access Group is associated with exactly one application record—this is a strict one-to-one relationship. An operator can belong to multiple access groups, and an access group can have multiple portals, but each access group points to only one application

Mock Exam 4.q: What does the Ruleset order in an application determine?
o: The deployment sequence for rulesets.
The order in which users are authenticated.
The hierarchy for rule resolution from most specific to least specific.
The order in which portals are loaded.
Mock Exam 4.r: Ruleset order in the application stack determines rule resolution priority. When Pega searches for a rule, it traverses the ruleset list from top (most specific) to bottom (least specific), using the first matching rule found. This enables layered customization and reuse

Mock Exam 4.q: A healthcare application must prevent nurses from viewing patient billing amounts in a case while allowing billing staff full visibility. What is the most appropriate configuration?
o: Use a when condition to hide the billing field based on the logged-in user's name
Create separate case types for nurses and billing staff with distinct views
Configure a field-level access policy to restrict the billing amount field for the nurse access role
Remove the billing section from the nurse work queue configuration
Mock Exam 4.r: Field-level access policies in Pega restrict visibility or editability of specific properties based on access roles, providing granular role-based security without duplicating case types or views

Mock Exam 4.q: Which Pega feature should you use to ensure that sensitive personal data, such as a credit card number, is encrypted when stored in the Pega database?
o: Use a data transform to hash the value before the case is submitted
Apply a when condition to hide the field after the case is submitted
Create a validate rule that checks the field value before saving
Configure the property's storage type to use encrypted storage
Mock Exam 4.r: Pega supports encrypting sensitive property values at the storage level by configuring the property's storage type. This ensures the data is protected in the database without requiring custom hashing or data transform logic

Mock Exam 4.q: You have designed a decision tree and want to unit test it with various input values. How do you unit test your decision tree?
o: Check the decision tree for completeness.
Run the decision tree and enter values on the test page.
Add the decision tree to a decision shape and create cases with various input values.
Check the decision tree for conflicts.
Mock Exam 4.r: Decision Trees have a built-in test page accessible from the rule form. You can enter property values directly and run the tree to see the returned result, making it easy to validate all branches without creating full cases

Mock Exam 4.q: While preparing to release an application, you notice a guardrail violation on an activity that copies order content. How do you address this guardrail violation?
o: Identify an API activity to use in place of the activity you wrote.
Ignore the warning if the compliance score is 90 or greater.
Replace the activity with a data transform to copy the content of the previous order.
Justify the warning since an activity is required in this situation.
Mock Exam 4.r: Guardrail violations should be resolved, not justified or ignored. Copying data between pages is precisely what Data Transforms are designed for. Replacing the activity with a Data Transform resolves the guardrail, improves maintainability, and follows Pega best practices

Mock Exam 4.q: Which statement is true about Pega Guardrails?
o: Guardrails have little or no impact on application performance.
Guardrails only apply to Activities and Data Transforms.
Guardrails must always be resolved before an application can be deployed.
Guardrails are enforced automatically and block rule saving.
Mock Exam 4.r: Guardrails are advisory best-practice warnings—they do not block rule saving or deployment. However, they indicate patterns that may cause performance or maintainability issues. Applications can be deployed with guardrail warnings, but resolving them is strongly recommended

Mock Exam 4.q: A hotel reservation application requires users to select a destination city from a list that narrows as the user types. Which UI control implements this?
o: Drop-down.
List to List.
Menu.
AutoComplete.
Mock Exam 4.r: AutoComplete is designed for large dynamic lists that filter as the user types. Drop-downs display a fixed list without filtering. AutoComplete also supports data page sources, making it ideal for city searches that may have hundreds of options

Mock Exam 4.q: Users access an apartment search application from desktop and smartphones. Photos show inline on wide screens but should stack vertically on smartphones. How do you implement this?
o: Use a column layout with a responsive breakpoint to hide left and right columns.
Circumstance the layout to display photos differently at different screen sizes.
Use a dynamic layout with a responsive breakpoint to change from inline to stacked format.
Circumstance the section rule to display photos differently at different screen sizes.
Mock Exam 4.r: Dynamic layouts in Pega support responsive breakpoints that automatically switch between inline and stacked formats based on screen width. This is the built-in, supported approach for responsive design. Circumstancing section rules adds unnecessary complexity

Mock Exam 4.q: To which principle does the UI layer of the Pega Constellation architecture subscribe?
o: Single Responsibility.
Architecture Hierarchy.
Separation of Concerns.
User Control and Consistency.
Mock Exam 4.r: Pega Constellation's UI layer follows the Separation of Concerns principle, decoupling UI components from business logic. This allows the UI layer to evolve independently, swap rendering engines, and support multiple channels without changing underlying case logic

Mock Exam 4.q: A customer views a product available in multiple color options and must select only one color. Which control presents all color choices at once while ensuring only one can be selected?
o: Radio buttons.
Check box.
Text input.
Drop-down.
Mock Exam 4.r: Radio buttons display all options simultaneously and enforce single selection by design. A drop-down also enforces single selection but hides options until clicked. Radio buttons are preferred when the list is short and users benefit from seeing all choices at once

Mock Exam 4.q: An application allows users to optionally add substitute transportation reimbursement. Users selecting this option must then see three reimbursement level radio buttons. How do you show the radio buttons only when the option is selected?
o: Add a refresh when condition on the check box control.
Add a visible when condition on the radio button control.
Add a validate rule to the flow action.
Add a validate rule to the check box control.
Mock Exam 4.r: A Visible When condition on the radio button control evaluates whether the check box is selected and shows or hides the radio buttons accordingly. This is a client-side visibility rule, providing a seamless real-time user experience without a round trip

Mock Exam 4.q: You are implementing a UI form collecting job applicant information. Users must provide values to certain fields before submitting. Which configuration adds asterisks to indicate mandatory fields?
o: Configure the mandatory fields as Required in the section rule.
Use multiple Edit Validate rules for each mandatory field.
Use an Edit Validate rule to verify if each mandatory property has a value.
Use a Validate rule to verify the mandatory fields have a value.
Mock Exam 4.r: Setting a field as Required in the section rule automatically adds the asterisk (*) indicator and prevents form submission if the field is empty. This is the correct, declarative approach. Validate rules run on submit but do not add visual indicators

Mock Exam 4.q: While preparing to release an application, you notice a guardrail violation on an activity that copies a customer's shipping address to their billing address. How do you address this?
o: Replace the activity with a data transform to copy the shipping address to the billing address.
Justify the warning, since an activity is required in this situation.
Ignore the warning if the compliance score is 90 or greater.
Identify an API activity to use in place of the activity you wrote.
Mock Exam 4.r: Copying data between pages is the core use case for Data Transforms. Using an Activity for this purpose violates guardrails. Replacing it with a Data Transform resolves the violation and aligns with Pega best practices for guardrail-compliant development

Mock Exam 4.q: Which issue is identified as a Guardrail violation?
o: A property in a report has not been optimized.
A decision tree contains a branch that cannot be reached.
An activity writes to the wrong clipboard page.
A decision table returns an invalid connector name to a flow.
Mock Exam 4.r: Pega Guardrails specifically flag report properties that have not been optimized (indexed) for performance. While the other options represent logic errors, they are not categorized as Guardrail violations in the Pega compliance scoring framework

Mock Exam 4.q: In which situation does a case type for software upgrade requests reuse a rule through pattern inheritance?
o: The case type uses an authorization process used throughout the organization.
The case type uses a data type defined in the Data- class.
The case type uses the Data-Party-Operator class to describe a work party.
The case type has a section rule with the same name as a section in the base class.
Mock Exam 4.r: Pattern inheritance occurs when a class reuses a rule from a parent class that has the same rule name. If the software upgrade case type uses an authorization flow defined on the organization's base Work class without overriding it, that is pattern inheritance

Mock Exam 4.q: A Service Request case type has a CustomerGrade property. How do you set its value to Silver when a service request case is created?
o: Configure a declare expression to set the CustomerGrade property value.
Configure the pyDefault data transform to set the CustomerGrade property value.
Configure the first connector in the first rule to set CustomerGrade.
Configure the CustomerGrade property with a default value.
Mock Exam 4.r: The pyDefault Data Transform runs automatically when a new case is created, making it the correct place to initialize property values. Setting a default directly on the property only provides a fallback, while pyDefault runs guaranteed at case creation

Mock Exam 4.q: In which situation is the use of an activity necessary?
o: Concatenating two string values.
Setting default values when creating a case.
Calculating the age from the date of birth.
Writing a message to a log file.
Mock Exam 4.r: Writing to a log file requires calling system-level API functions that cannot be replicated with Data Transforms or Declare Expressions. This is one of the few valid use cases for Activities in modern Pega development. All other listed tasks have guardrail-compliant alternatives

Mock Exam 4.q: The application contains case type ORG-App-Work-PurchaseOrder using an embedded page of class ORG-App-Data-Customer. What is the most appropriate 'Applies To' class for a section rule displaying customer information?
o: ORG-App-Work.
ORG-App-Data-Customer.
ORG-App-Work-PurchaseOrder.
ORG-App-Data.
Mock Exam 4.r: The section rule should apply to the class of the page it will render. Since the customer data is on a page of class ORG-App-Data-Customer, the section must apply to that class for correct property resolution and reuse across other case types that use the same data class

Mock Exam 4.q: While testing a form, you need to verify the contents of a data page in memory. Which tool do you use to view the current contents of the data page?
o: Live UI.
The Tracer.
The Clipboard tool.
The Data Explorer.
Mock Exam 4.r: The Clipboard tool in the Dev Studio toolbar displays all pages currently in memory for the active requestor, including data pages and their property values. The Tracer shows rule execution history; Live UI shows section/control rule names

Mock Exam 4.q: While reviewing a UI form in a Grooming/Elaboration playback, you notice a typo in a field label. Which tool allows you to identify the section rule containing the incorrect label?
o: The Clipboard tool.
The Property Analyzer.
Live UI.
The Tracer.
Mock Exam 4.r: Live UI overlays rule names directly onto the rendered UI, enabling developers to click on any element to identify the exact section or control rule responsible for it. This makes it the fastest way to locate the source of a UI issue without navigating rule hierarchies manually

Mock Exam 4.q: Which two statements are true about the Localization wizard? (Choose two)
o: You can use it to change the locale, base currency, and time zone.
You can use it to verify if the localization flag is enabled on user interface Rules.
You can use it to export strings to be translated containing Rules such as field value or message Rules.
You can use it to export Correspondence and Paragraph Rules as HTML files to be translated.
Mock Exam 4.r: The Localization wizard exports translatable strings from Field Value and Message rules as well as Correspondence and Paragraph rules as HTML files for external translation. It does not change locale settings (that is done in the application record) or validate UI localization flags

Mock Exam 4.q: You want to configure your dashboard to include work volume by status. How do you achieve this?
o: Update your dashboard to include the Work Volume by Status widget.
Create a new Dashboard landing page using the Work Volume by Status page template.
Update your dashboard template from Wide-narrow.
Create a Work Volume by Status landing page to add to your dashboard landing page.
Mock Exam 4.r: Pega dashboards are built by adding widgets to an existing dashboard layout. The Work Volume by Status widget is a pre-built dashboard component that displays case volume grouped by status. Adding a widget is simpler than creating new landing pages

Mock Exam 4.q: A manager requests a report showing Create Date, Case ID, Create Operator, and Work Status. Cases should be sorted with the most recent create date at the top. How do you design the report?
o: Add a filter condition where Create Date is greater than the current date.
Select Count in the Summarize column for Create Date.
Select Highest to Lowest sort type for Create Date.
Make Create Date the first column in the report.
Mock Exam 4.r: Sorting Highest to Lowest on a date column arranges records from the most recent date descending. Adding it as the first column only affects display order, not sort order. The Summarize column is for grouping/aggregation, not sorting

Mock Exam 4.q: You have a report with employees, hire dates, and managers. You need to display each manager in a row with their employees listed beneath. How do you implement this?
o: Sort the manager column.
Summarize the manager column.
Group the manager column.
Filter the manager column.
Mock Exam 4.r: Grouping the manager column creates a hierarchical report layout where each distinct manager appears as a group header with their employees listed underneath. Sorting alone would order the rows but not create the visual group structure with indented child rows

Mock Exam 4.q: A developer adds a Send Email step to a case life cycle and wants generative AI to draft an appropriate email message for that step automatically. Which Pega GenAI feature supports this?
o: Knowledge Buddy
Pega GenAI Coach
Pega GenAI Autopilot
Pega GenAI Blueprint
Mock Exam 4.r: Pega GenAI Autopilot is a design-time assistant in App Studio that can generate content suggestions, including drafting email message templates for Send Email steps based on the step's context within the case life cycle

Mock Exam 4.q: In which Pega studio is Pega GenAI Autopilot primarily available to assist developers during application building?
o: Dev Studio
App Studio
Prediction Studio
Admin Studio
Mock Exam 4.r: Pega GenAI Autopilot is integrated into App Studio as a design-time AI assistant, providing suggestions and generating content directly within the low-code environment where developers build case types, stages, and data models

Mock Exam 4.q: A company wants to allow customers on a self-service portal to ask natural-language questions about account status, product features, and company policies, receiving answers drawn from internal documents. Which Pega GenAI feature should be configured?
o: Pega GenAI Coach
Knowledge Buddy
Pega GenAI Autopilot
Pega GenAI Blueprint
Mock Exam 4.r: Knowledge Buddy is designed to answer natural-language questions by querying configured knowledge sources (company documents, PDFs, URLs). It is suitable for customer-facing portals where users need fast, accurate answers without switching systems

Mock Exam 4.q: What must be configured to make Knowledge Buddy answers specific to a company's products and internal policies?
o: A data page sourced from an external document management system
Company-specific knowledge sources such as documents, PDFs, and URLs added to the Knowledge Buddy configuration
A machine learning model trained on historical customer support tickets
Access roles that authorize users to query the knowledge base
Mock Exam 4.r: Knowledge Buddy derives its answers from the knowledge sources configured for it. Adding company-specific documents, PDFs, and URLs is what makes the responses relevant to the organization's particular context, rather than general knowledge

Mock Exam 4.q: What output does Pega GenAI Blueprint produce after a business user submits a natural-language application description?
o: A production-ready Pega application packaged for immediate deployment
A set of integration rules connecting Pega to external AI service providers
A structured application blueprint with suggested case types, lifecycle stages, data fields, and automations ready for refinement
An automated test suite with pre-built assertions for each case stage
Mock Exam 4.r: Pega GenAI Blueprint converts a business description into an initial structured design — including case types, stages, fields, and automations — that the development team can then review, refine, and implement. It produces a starting point, not a finished application

Mock Exam 4.q: Which two Pega GenAI features operate at design time to assist application developers?
o: Knowledge Buddy
Pega GenAI Blueprint
Pega GenAI Autopilot
Pega GenAI Coach
Mock Exam 4.r: Autopilot assists developers in App Studio by suggesting case types, fields, and content. Blueprint converts a business description into an application design. Coach and Knowledge Buddy are runtime features for end users processing cases, not design-time tools

Mock Exam 5.q: A loan application moves through Submission, Underwriting, Approval, and Funding stages. In Pega Case Designer, how should each of these business milestones be represented?
o: Stages
Processes
Case types
Steps
Mock Exam 5.r: Stages represent major business milestones in a case life cycle. Each stage (Submission, Underwriting, Approval, Funding) is a high-level phase of work. Within each stage, processes contain the individual steps assigned to operators

Mock Exam 5.q: Which best describes a case type in Pega Platform?
o: A reusable template that defines how a category of work is processed end to end.
A class group used only for reporting.
A decision strategy that scores customers.
A user interface portal definition.
Mock Exam 5.r: A case type is a template that defines the full lifecycle—stages, steps, data, routing, and SLAs—for a repeatable category of business work. Every time a user creates a case, Pega instantiates a new copy of the case type template

Mock Exam 5.q: You want a case to automatically advance to the next stage as soon as the last step in the current stage completes, with no human action required. Which stage transition should you configure?
o: On stage entry
Manual
Wait
Automatic
Mock Exam 5.r: The Automatic transition moves a case to the next stage immediately when all work in the current stage is complete, without requiring an operator to click a button. Manual transition requires a human action; Wait pauses for an external event

Mock Exam 5.q: An assignment must be completed within 8 business hours, with a goal at 4 hours and a deadline at 8 hours. Which Pega rule type configures this time-based requirement?
o: Service level agreement (SLA).
Decision table.
When rule.
Activity.
Mock Exam 5.r: An SLA defines time-based goals and deadlines for completing an assignment or case. The goal (4 hours) is the target, the deadline (8 hours) is the last-resort threshold. Escalation actions (notifications, reassignments) can fire at each interval

Mock Exam 5.q: Which option BEST describes an Approve/Reject step in a Pega case life cycle?
o: It runs only as a background activity.
It creates an assignment whose result drives the next process.
It can only be used in the Resolve stage.
It always invokes a sub case.
Mock Exam 5.r: An Approve/Reject step creates an assignment for a decision maker. When the operator selects Approve or Reject, the outcome drives which path the case takes next in the flow. It is a human-facing routing mechanism

Mock Exam 5.q: A parent Insurance Claim case must spawn one Vehicle Damage child case per damaged vehicle and wait for all of them to resolve before continuing. Which Pega construct should you use?
o: Assignment routing.
Child cases with a wait step.
Spin-off case.
Optional process.
Mock Exam 5.r: Creating child cases and adding a Wait step configured to wait until all child cases reach Resolved status is the correct pattern. The wait step pauses the parent case until all dependencies are satisfied before continuing

Mock Exam 5.q: Which routing option would BEST direct an assignment to any available agent in a specific work group?
o: Current operator.
Specific user only.
Workbasket associated with the work group.
Manager of the case creator.
Mock Exam 5.r: A Workbasket is a shared queue where multiple operators can pull work. Routing to the workbasket associated with a work group makes the assignment available to any qualified agent in that group, enabling pull routing

Mock Exam 5.q: Which behavior occurs when an assignment passes its SLA deadline without being completed?
o: Nothing happens until the next agent is run manually.
The configured passed-deadline escalation actions run.
The case is automatically resolved.
Pega rolls the case back to the previous stage.
Mock Exam 5.r: When a deadline passes, Pega executes the escalation actions configured in the SLA rule (e.g., send email, reassign, change urgency). The case is not automatically resolved or rolled back—business logic in the escalation actions determines the response

Mock Exam 5.q: A business analyst wants users to launch an optional Address Update process from any stage of the case, without interrupting the primary workflow. Which construct supports this?
o: Automatic stage transition.
Stage-only process.
Sub case in the Resolve stage.
Optional action available across stages.
Mock Exam 5.r: A case-wide optional action (available across all stages) allows operators to trigger a secondary process at any time without affecting the primary case flow. It appears in the Actions menu and does not block stage progression

Mock Exam 5.q: An organization allows time-off requests that normally require only manager approval. Requests exceeding three weeks require approval from a manager, director, and HR. Which two configurations support multi-level approval for the extended requests? (Choose two)
o: Use a cascading approval with a reporting structure.
Use a cascading approval with an authority matrix.
Create a decision table and evaluate all rows.
Configure custom approvals in the reporting structure.
Mock Exam 5.r: Cascading approvals route through multiple levels sequentially. An authority matrix allows explicit mapping of approvers by criteria (e.g., request duration). A reporting structure routes approvals through the operator's org hierarchy. Both satisfy multi-level, multi-condition approval requirements

Mock Exam 5.q: A job application process includes steps where a recruiter notifies the candidate and schedules an interview. Which two step names follow Pega naming guidelines for steps? (Choose two)
o: Ask Questions.
Notify Candidate.
Technical Exercise.
Schedule Interview.
Mock Exam 5.r: Pega step naming guidelines prescribe action-verb + noun phrases (e.g., 'Notify Candidate', 'Schedule Interview'). 'Ask Questions' is too vague and 'Technical Exercise' is a noun phrase that does not describe an action performed by the system or operator

Mock Exam 5.q: An airline application prompts a passenger for service animal details (type, size, medical info) only when the passenger declares travel with a service animal. Which case life cycle configuration meets this requirement?
o: Create a child case for service animal accommodation that auto-resolves if not needed.
Configure a stage with a validation condition for service animal accommodation.
Add a process to the case life cycle for service animal accommodation and apply a condition to determine when to run the process.
Apply an optional action to the stage for service animal accommodation.
Mock Exam 5.r: Adding a conditional process to the case life cycle that runs only when the service animal flag is set is the correct pattern. The condition (when rule) gates whether the process executes. Optional actions require operator initiation; a separate stage would be unnecessarily complex

Mock Exam 5.q: A Visa case type creates an Interview child case. The Visa case must wait for the Interview case to be fully resolved before continuing to the notification stage. How do you configure this behavior?
o: Add an SLA that escalates the parent case after 48 hours.
Add an Interview step that is automatically resolved after 48 hours.
Add a Wait step that pauses the parent case until the application schedules the interview.
Add a Wait step that pauses the parent case until the Interview case reaches the Resolved status.
Mock Exam 5.r: A Wait step configured with a case dependency (wait until child case reaches Resolved status) pauses the parent Visa case until the Interview child case is fully processed. This is the standard Pega pattern for parent-child case synchronization

Mock Exam 5.q: A music studio allows clients to upload audio recordings before a consultation. The studio wants to pause case processing after Client Intake and give clients 72 hours to upload recordings. Which configuration meets this requirement?
o: Configure a child case to upload recordings; add a Wait step with a case dependency until the child case is resolved.
Configure a service level on the stage with a deadline of 72 hours.
Configure a validate rule on the Client Intake stage with elapsed time set to 72 hours.
Configure a case-wide optional action for uploads and add a Wait shape with a Timer Wait type set to 72 hours.
Mock Exam 5.r: A Timer Wait step pauses the case for a specified duration (72 hours) after which processing automatically continues. Adding an optional action for the upload allows clients to submit recordings during that window. An SLA deadline alone would only escalate, not pause

Mock Exam 5.q: An accident claim case creates a Vehicle Claim child case for each vehicle involved. Which two configurations prevent the accident claim from resolving before all vehicle claim cases are resolved? (Choose two)
o: Add each vehicle claim as a child case of the accident claim.
Add an optional process to pause the accident case until vehicle claims are paid.
Add a manual approval step to the accident claim case.
Add a wait step to the accident claim case to wait until all vehicle claims have a status of Resolved.
Mock Exam 5.r: Combining child case creation with a Wait step (wait until all child cases reach Resolved) is the correct pattern. Pega tracks child case status automatically when they are created as children of the parent, and the wait step enforces the dependency before the parent can resolve

Mock Exam 5.q: A bookseller application allows users to select a book title from a catalog of more than 10,000 titles. Which control and data source configuration should you use?
o: Add an autocomplete control sourcing data from the clipboard.
Add an autocomplete control sourcing data using a data page.
Add a drop-down control sourcing data using a data page.
Add a drop-down control sourcing data from a property value.
Mock Exam 5.r: An AutoComplete control with a data page source is the recommended approach for large dynamic lists. AutoComplete filters as the user types, making searches across thousands of records manageable. A drop-down would render all 10,000+ options at once, which is a performance and usability problem
