Child Cases can run in parallel, reducing total processing time
Mock Exam 1.r: Child Cases enable parallelism (different teams work simultaneously) and independent ownership with their own SLAs and data. They do not automatically merge, and each child Case can have its own routing/queues, not a shared Worklist.

Mock Exam 1.q: What is the correct Pega naming convention for a Stage in a Case Life Cycle?
o: A verb + noun (e.g., 'Process order')
A noun, noun phrase, or gerund of up to two words (e.g., 'Processing')
An outcome statement (e.g., 'Loan Application Review')
A numeric identifier (e.g., 'Stage 1')
Mock Exam 1.r: Stages use a noun, noun phrase, or gerund of up to two words, such as 'Processing' or 'Delivery.' Verb + noun is the convention for Processes and Steps; outcome statements name Case Types; numeric IDs are not a recommended convention.

Mock Exam 1.q: A Data Transform rule is used to copy billing address values to shipping address fields. Which concept best describes this capability?
o: A validation rule that rejects invalid field entries
An Automation Step that sends an email
A calculated value field derived from a formula
A rule that sets, copies, and transforms data values between pages and fields
Mock Exam 1.r: A Data Transform is a rule that manipulates data by setting, copying, and transforming values between pages/fields — ideal for seeding defaults or copying address data. Validation rules check correctness; calculated fields derive values; Automation Steps perform system actions.

Mock Exam 1.q: Which description best fits the Pulse feature in Pega Platform?
o: A validation rule that enforces mandatory fields
A chart visualization tool for Case analytics
A routing engine that assigns work to operators
A collaboration feed that lets team members post, comment, and reply in context on a Case or feature
Mock Exam 1.r: Pulse is an in-context collaboration feed where team members post messages, comment, and reply directly within a Case or feature — keeping conversations tied to the work. It is not a chart tool, routing engine, or validation mechanism.

Mock Exam 1.q: A Promoted Action button appears in the Case header giving operators instant access to a key action. How many Promoted Actions can each Case Type support, and which action is automatically used?
o: Up to five Promoted Actions per Case Type, selected by the operator at runtime
Unlimited Promoted Actions, limited only by the number of Access Roles
One Promoted Action per Stage, configured individually for each Stage
One Promoted Action per Case Type; the first Case-wide Action becomes the Promoted Action automatically
Mock Exam 1.r: Each Case Type supports exactly ONE Promoted Action displayed on the Case header. The first Case-wide Action is automatically designated as the Promoted Action, giving operators quick access without requiring additional buttons.

Mock Exam 1.q: In the Conceptual Data Model, what are the three elements used to describe data?
o: Entities, Attributes, and Relationships
Data objects, Fields, and Data Pages
Tables, Columns, and Foreign Keys
Classes, Properties, and Rulesets
Mock Exam 1.r: The Conceptual Data Model uses Entities, Attributes, and Relationships — business-facing terms built with stakeholders. Data objects and Fields belong to the Logical model; Classes/Properties are Pega platform terms; Tables/Columns are physical database terms.

Mock Exam 1.q: In Pega's App Studio, a data object's fields are called 'fields.' What are these same constructs called in Dev Studio?
o: Dimensions
Attributes
Properties
Columns
Mock Exam 1.r: In Dev Studio, what App Studio calls a 'field' is called a 'property.' The underlying structure is identical; only the terminology differs between the two studios. Similarly, a 'data object' in App Studio is a 'data type' in Dev Studio.

Mock Exam 1.q: A customer enters credit card details directly into each order form — data unique to that specific order. Which relationship type and cardinality should be configured?
o: Embedded Data, List of records
Case reference, Single record
Data reference, Single record
Embedded Data, Single record
Mock Exam 1.r: Data typed directly into the Case instance (not from a shared record) uses Embedded Data. Because only one credit card exists per order, the cardinality is Single record. Data reference is for data from an external or local system of record.

Mock Exam 1.q: A Customer object is maintained in an external CRM system, and each order references exactly one customer. Which relationship configuration is correct?
o: Data reference, List of records
Case reference, List of records
Embedded Data, Single record
Data reference, Single record
Mock Exam 1.r: Data from an external system of record uses Data reference (not Embedded). One customer per order means Single record cardinality. Case reference is for sourcing data from another Case Type; List of records applies when multiple instances exist.

Mock Exam 1.q: What is the role of a Data Page in Pega Platform?
o: It permanently stores Case data in the Pega database
It acts as a bridge that retrieves data from a source and caches it in memory, decoupling the Case from the underlying storage
It defines the schema of external database tables
It is a UI layout template for displaying data
Mock Exam 1.r: A Data Page retrieves data from a configured source and caches it for use, forming the Pega Live Data virtualization layer that decouples business logic from storage details. It is not a permanent store, schema definition, or UI template.

Mock Exam 1.q: How many default Data Pages does each data object in Pega have, and what types are they?
o: One: a single read-and-write
Two: both read-only
Three: a single read-only, a list read-only, and a single read-and-write (savable)
Four: including two savable pages
Mock Exam 1.r: Each data object has three default Data Pages: single read-only, list read-only, and single read-and-write (savable). Case Types have only two default Data Pages (both read-only) because Cases auto-save.

Mock Exam 1.q: Which TWO statements correctly describe Attended and Unattended RPA in Pega?
o: Attended RPA drives a legacy UI in real time alongside a human operator during a live interaction
Attended RPA queues work for later processing during off-peak hours
Unattended RPA places requests in a queue for background processing to optimize system resources
Unattended RPA requires a human to approve each action in real time
Mock Exam 1.r: Attended RPA runs in real time with a human in the loop (e.g., a CSR triggers a robot mid-call). Unattended RPA places requests in a queue for background processing, reducing peak loads. The other options invert these definitions.

Mock Exam 1.q: Pega Blueprint is a standalone SaaS tool. What does this mean for business stakeholders who want to collaborate on application design?
o: Blueprint requires PremBridge to operate
They can co-design without a Pega instance or login; Blueprint runs independently of Pega Platform
They must each have a Pega operator account to participate
Blueprint runs inside Dev Studio only
Mock Exam 1.r: Blueprint is a standalone SaaS tool at pega.com/blueprint; business stakeholders can collaborate without a Pega login. Those with a Pega login can still join. It does not run inside Dev Studio and PremBridge is not required.

Mock Exam 1.q: A developer uses Pega GenAI Autopilot during application design to get real-time suggestions for Case Types, Data Model fields, and Personas. At which phase does Autopilot operate?
o: Testing time (during QA only)
Deployment time (when promoting to production)
Run time (while end users work Cases)
Design time (inside App Studio)
Mock Exam 1.r: Autopilot operates at design time, covering all generative AI features available inside App Studio during application building. Coach and Agent/Tool Rules operate at run time. Deployment and QA are separate phases.

Mock Exam 1.q: A Connect Generative AI Step returns a short, single structured object that maps to one field in the Data Model. Which response structure should be selected?
o: Structured - Single
Unstructured
Encrypted - Binary
Structured - List
Mock Exam 1.r: Structured-Single maps a single LLM-returned object to a Data Model field. Structured-List is for multiple objects mapped to a page list; Unstructured (raw text) maps to a Text paragraph field. Encrypted-Binary is not a valid GenAI Connect response structure.

Mock Exam 1.q: Which TWO items can Pega GenAI Autopilot generate during application design?
o: Compiled Java code for the application
Sample data records for a data object to ease testing
Case Types including a suggested Case Life Cycle and Data Model
Production database server hardware configurations
Mock Exam 1.r: Autopilot generates Case Types (with Life Cycle and Data Model) and sample data records/form-fill for testing. It does not provision hardware or compile Java code. All Autopilot suggestions should be reviewed before accepting.

Mock Exam 1.q: A Pega GenAI Agent governed by Tool Rules can perform which type of action at run time?
o: Generate machine-learning models in Prediction Studio
Design the Case Life Cycle in Blueprint
Run an automation, start a Case, call another agent, or extract data from an uploaded document
Configure the Ruleset stack for deployment
Mock Exam 1.r: GenAI Agents automate Case processing at run time: they can run automations, start Cases, call other agents, launch user actions, and extract data from uploaded documents. Blueprint and Autopilot are design-time tools; Prediction Studio handles ML models.

Mock Exam 1.q: What software design principle does the Pega UI layer apply to keep front-end components decoupled from back-end APIs?
o: Separation of Concerns
Center-out architecture
Pattern inheritance
Model-driven UI
Mock Exam 1.r: The Pega UI layer applies Separation of Concerns — dividing the application into distinct parts, each with a single responsibility, so UI components are decoupled from business logic and back-end APIs. Model-driven UI and Center-out are related but distinct concepts.

Mock Exam 1.q: A portal in Pega Platform is composed of which three regions?
o: Header, Navigation, and Landing Pages
Rules, Classes, and Rulesets
Stages, Processes, and Steps
Data objects, Fields, and Relationships
Mock Exam 1.r: A portal is structured with a Header (logo, search, utilities), Navigation (menus for moving between areas), and Landing Pages/dashboards (the main content area). Stages/Processes/Steps are Case Life Cycle building blocks; the others are Data Model and Rules concepts.

Mock Exam 1.q: A BA configures a field to display in red highlighting only when its value exceeds a limit, without changing the stored value. Which UI capability achieves this?
o: Dynamic visibility
A template layout
A Promoted Action
Conditional formatting / control styling at runtime
Mock Exam 1.r: Conditional formatting (control styling) changes how a control is displayed at run time based on conditions — such as highlighting an overdue value — without altering the stored field value. Dynamic visibility shows/hides elements; Promoted Actions and templates serve different purposes.

Mock Exam 1.q: A 'Reason for rejection' field should only appear in the form when the Decision field is set to 'Rejected.' Which UI capability controls this?
o: A Promoted Action — a quick-access button on the Case header
Conditional formatting — changing a control's color
A template — controlling layout and responsiveness
Dynamic visibility — showing or hiding elements based on a condition
Mock Exam 1.r: Dynamic visibility controls whether a field or UI element is shown or hidden based on a runtime condition, such as Decision = Rejected. Conditional formatting changes appearance; Promoted Actions add header buttons; templates manage layout.

Mock Exam 1.q: Which TWO are correct statements about the Pega UI design system (Cosmos React)?
o: Templates handle layout and responsiveness including breakpoints and white-space management
It is a prescribed, systemized collection of design rules and UI component standards that ensures consistent look, feel, and accessibility
Templates are optional and have no effect on accessibility
The design system requires hand-coding CSS for every screen
Mock Exam 1.r: Cosmos React is Pega's prescribed design system ensuring consistency and accessibility. Templates handle layout, responsiveness, and breakpoints and include out-of-the-box accessibility. Templates are mandatory for View layout, not optional, and no hand-coded CSS is required.

Mock Exam 1.q: A BA wants to visualize the number of Cases created per day over the last month to spot trends at a glance. Which type of Insight should they create?
o: Chart Insight (bar, line, or pie chart)
Table Insight (rows and columns)
BIX extraction
A Data Transform
Mock Exam 1.r: A Chart Insight renders query results as a visualization (bar, line, or pie chart) — ideal for spotting trends, comparisons, and distributions. A Table Insight shows detailed row-level data; BIX extracts data to external BI tools; a Data Transform manipulates field values.

Mock Exam 1.q: An enterprise needs to extract millions of Pega Case records nightly into an external data warehouse for cross-system reporting. Which capability is most appropriate?
o: Pega Insights
The Explore Data landing page
BIX (Business Intelligence Exchange)
A Savable Data Page
Mock Exam 1.r: BIX is Pega's data extract capability for pulling application data into external databases or BI tools at scale. Insights analyze data within Pega; the Explore Data landing page is where you build Insights; a Savable Data Page writes individual records back to a source.

Mock Exam 1.q: From which App Studio area do business users access the Insights and data analysis capabilities?
o: The Users section
The Library (Reuse Library)
The Explore Data landing page
The Channels section
Mock Exam 1.r: Insights are built and accessed from the Explore Data landing page in App Studio. The Library holds reusable assets; Channels configures web/mobile portals; Users manages operator setup. Explore Data is the dedicated analytics entry point.

Mock Exam 1.q: A newly onboarded employee logs into Pega for the first time. The system confirms their identity with a username/password check. Which security concept does this represent?
o: Authentication — verifying who the user is
Access Role assignment
Persona configuration
Authorization — determining what the user can do
Mock Exam 1.r: Authentication verifies WHO the user is — confirming identity at login (username/password, SSO, MFA). Authorization happens after authentication to determine WHAT the authenticated user is allowed to access via Access Roles and Access Groups.

Mock Exam 1.q: In Pega's security model, which construct defines WHAT a user is permitted to do — permissions to classes and actions — and is granted via the Access Group?
o: Access Role
Persona
Operator record
Work Queue
Mock Exam 1.r: An Access Role defines what a user is permitted to do (RBAC permissions to classes and actions) and is granted via the Access Group. A Persona is the role category; the Operator record stores the user's profile; a Work Queue is a routing construct, not a security one.

Mock Exam 2.q: A BA teaches stakeholders about Pega's out-of-the-box automatic routing and email notifications, helping them see the value and become advocates for the new process. Which core BA responsibility does this describe?
o: Education
Analysis
Process Design
Alignment
Mock Exam 2.r: Teaching stakeholders the value of Pega OOTB features and enabling them to change their ways of working is Education — the ongoing responsibility of the BA throughout the project. Analysis diagnoses the current process; Process Design optimizes via Blueprint; Alignment collaborates to build.

Mock Exam 2.q: Which of the four Pega studios provides runtime information for monitoring and debugging system resources, intended for IT administrators?
o: Admin Studio
App Studio
Prediction Studio
Dev Studio
Mock Exam 2.r: Admin Studio is the software administration space for system monitoring and debugging at runtime, managed by IT administrators. App Studio is the core authoring space; Dev Studio handles advanced configuration; Prediction Studio is for analytics/ML models.

Mock Exam 2.q: A System Architect needs to configure an integration service with a complex security mechanism unavailable in App Studio. According to best practice, where should this be configured?
o: Dev Studio — used for advanced features and complex configuration not available in App Studio
Prediction Studio — for security analytics
App Studio — always use it regardless of feature availability
Admin Studio — for all integration work
Mock Exam 2.r: Best practice is to use App Studio unless a required feature is unavailable there. Complex integrations and advanced security are Dev Studio features. Admin Studio is for system administration; Prediction Studio is for ML/analytics models.

Mock Exam 2.q: Which capability allows a business user to update a threshold rule (such as an auto-approval limit) without filing an IT change request, while leaving the rest of the application unchanged?
o: Rule Parametrization
Rule Reuse
Rule Delegation
Rule Versioning
Mock Exam 2.r: Delegation exposes a specific rule to business users so they can update Case behavior (e.g., adjust a threshold) without an IT change request or touching other rules. Versioning maintains history/rollback; Reuse applies existing behavior; Parametrization is a design technique to drive logic with passed values.

Mock Exam 2.q: Which TWO correctly pair a Pega Platform UI architecture with its Ruleset?
o: Traditional UI architecture uses the Theme Cosmos Ruleset and provides a Section-based UI
Traditional UI architecture uses the Constellation Ruleset
Constellation architecture uses the Constellation Ruleset and provides a View-based UI
Constellation architecture uses the Theme Cosmos Ruleset
Mock Exam 2.r: Constellation architecture pairs with the Constellation Ruleset and a View-based UI. Traditional UI architecture pairs with the Theme Cosmos Ruleset and a Section-based UI. Options C and D swap these pairings and are incorrect.

Mock Exam 2.q: What is the class hierarchy search order in Pega Platform at runtime?
o: Alphabetical order across all classes
Only within the class where the Case was created
From the most-specific class, expanding outward to more general parent classes
From the most-general class down to the most-specific
Mock Exam 2.r: Pega begins Rule resolution at the most-specific class and expands outward through parent classes up to @baseclass. If no Rule is found by @baseclass, Pega returns a Rule-not-found error. Resolution never goes top-down or randomly.

Mock Exam 2.q: Which Center-out benefit describes the result when a team defines business rules once in a central location to eliminate duplication and inconsistency across channels?
o: Efficiency
Agility
Scalability
Governance
Mock Exam 2.r: Efficiency = defining rules once centrally to eliminate duplication and reduce inconsistency. Agility = a rule change propagates automatically across all channels. Governance = centralized auditing/policy enforcement. Scalability = reusing logic as new touchpoints are added.

Mock Exam 2.q: A private individual development space tied to one operator and one application, whose changes remain hidden until shared, is called:
o: A Ruleset
A Branch
An Access Group
A Workspace
Mock Exam 2.r: A Workspace is tied to exactly one operator and one application; changes remain private until shared to a Branch. A Branch is the shared feature container for a team; a Ruleset stores and identifies Rules; an Access Group governs access.

Mock Exam 2.q: The Reuse Library in Pega Platform is located in which studio, and what is its purpose?
o: Admin Studio — for monitoring reusable component usage
App Studio — a centralized, governed repository of reusable assets for developers of all skill levels
Prediction Studio — for sharing ML models
Dev Studio — a repository visible only to System Architects
Mock Exam 2.r: The Reuse Library resides in App Studio and provides a centralized, governed catalog of reusable assets accessible to developers at all skill levels. It is not limited to System Architects, nor is it in Admin or Prediction Studio.

Mock Exam 2.q: Which guiding principle of modular enterprise reuse means that applications are assembled from encapsulated, self-contained units rather than built as large monolithic layers?
o: Interoperable
Governed
Modular
Configurable
Mock Exam 2.r: Modular means applications are assembled from encapsulated, self-contained components rather than large monolithic layers that are hard to maintain. Interoperable = consistent blocks across studios/apps; Configurable = adjust behavior without rewriting logic; Governed = Center of Excellence management.

Mock Exam 2.q: Which TWO Pega CI/CD best practices reduce risk when promoting application changes to production?
o: Run automated tests (unit and scenario) within the pipeline before promoting changes
Deploy all changes at once without staging environments
Develop features in Branches and merge only when stable, conflict-free, and approved
Edit rules directly in locked lower built-on applications
Mock Exam 2.r: Branch-based development isolates features until approved; automated testing catches defects early in the pipeline. Editing locked lower apps and skipping staging environments are anti-patterns that increase risk and are not recommended.

Mock Exam 2.q: In which tool does a BA document user stories using Blueprint and Pega's Agile tooling so System Architects can implement them?
o: Prediction Studio
Blueprint and App Studio's Agile Workbench
Dev Studio's class hierarchy
Admin Studio's monitoring dashboard
Mock Exam 2.r: BAs document requirements as user stories using Blueprint and App Studio's Agile Workbench. System Architects use those stories to size and configure. Prediction Studio, Admin Studio, and the class hierarchy serve entirely different purposes.

Mock Exam 2.q: Which statement correctly describes the top-down traditional software architecture approach?
o: Each system maintains its own siloed data view with no unified entity
Business logic is defined once and shared across all touchpoints
The same business logic must be implemented multiple times across different channels to keep them consistent
Channel-specific code is eliminated entirely
Mock Exam 2.r: Top-down architecture designs around the presentation/channel layer, requiring business logic to be duplicated for each channel. Data silos describe the bottom-up problem. Business logic defined once and shared is Center-out architecture.

Mock Exam 2.q: A Case Type represents which of the following?
o: An abstract model of a repeatable business transaction
A user persona who processes Cases
A specific numbered transaction instance
A stage in the Case Life Cycle
Mock Exam 2.r: A Case Type is the abstract, reusable model of a repeatable business transaction (the cookie cutter). A Case is a specific numbered instance of that model (the cookie). Stages are Case Life Cycle building blocks; Personas are user role categories.

Mock Exam 2.q: When should a Change Stage Automation Step be used in a Case Life Cycle?
o: To route an Assignment to a Work Queue
To automatically transition a Case to a specific Stage, such as moving into or out of an Alternate Stage based on a condition
To display a form for the user to fill in
To define the goal and deadline of an SLA
Mock Exam 2.r: A Change Stage Automation Step transitions the Case to a specific Stage automatically — most commonly used to move into and out of Alternate Stages. Displaying forms uses Collect information Steps; Work Queue routing is an Assignment configuration; SLA defines goal/deadline.

Mock Exam 2.q: Which option correctly lists all three pillars that define a Pega application in App Studio?
o: Worklists, Work Queues, and SLAs
Rules, Classes, and Rulesets
Stages, Processes, and Steps
Case Types & Strategies; Data & Interfaces; Personas & Channels
Mock Exam 2.r: The three pillars are Case Types & Strategies, Data & Interfaces, and Personas & Channels. Stages/Processes/Steps are Case Life Cycle building blocks; Rules/Classes/Rulesets are platform architecture; Worklists/Work Queues/SLAs are assignment and SLA concepts.

Mock Exam 2.q: Which TWO statements about the Create Stage in a Pega Case Life Cycle are correct?
o: Stage transitions can be configured on it like any other Stage
It cannot be deleted or repositioned, but it can be renamed
It can be moved to a position after the second Stage
It is displayed with a green bar and assigns the Case ID upon creation
Mock Exam 2.r: The Create Stage is always first (green bar), assigns the Case ID, cannot be deleted or repositioned (but can be renamed), and does NOT support Stage transitions. Moving it is impossible; Stage transitions apply only to non-Create Stages.

Mock Exam 2.q: A Microjourney is best described as:
o: The overall enterprise strategy for digital transformation
A Ruleset version naming convention
A unit of work that delivers a meaningful result, representing part of the overall customer journey tied to a specific outcome
A type of report generated in Insights
Mock Exam 2.r: A Microjourney is a unit of work delivering a meaningful result — a slice of the customer journey tied to a specific outcome, modeled as a Case Type in App Studio. It is not a strategy, Ruleset version, or report type.

Mock Exam 2.q: A BA is routing an assignment to the currently logged-in user. Which routing option does this represent?
o: Route to a specific named operator
Route to an Access Role
Route to current user (Worklist)
Route to a Work Queue (shared team queue)
Mock Exam 2.r: Routing to the current user sends the Assignment to that operator's personal Worklist. Routing to a Work Queue creates a shared pull-based queue for any qualified team member. Routing to a specific named operator always targets that person regardless of who is logged in.

Mock Exam 2.q: A user must select the assigned surgeon for a surgical procedure Case from a pre-approved list stored locally in the Pega database. What relationship type and cardinality should be used?
o: Embedded Data, Single record
Case reference, Single record
Embedded Data, List of records
Data reference, Single record
Mock Exam 2.r: Data sourced from a local Pega database record uses Data reference (not Embedded). One surgeon per procedure means Single record cardinality. Embedded is for data typed directly in the Case; Case reference sources data from another Case Type.

Mock Exam 2.q: A non-Channel-specific Create Process can only include which Step type?
o: Automation Steps only
Collect information Steps
Change Stage Steps only
Any Step type
Mock Exam 2.r: Non-Channel-specific Create Processes are restricted to Collect information Steps (user-action Steps for initial data entry). Automation Steps are deferred to post-creation; Change Stage Steps are not valid Create Process step types; no unrestricted mix is allowed.

Mock Exam 2.q: What is the business value of cross-functional Work Groups in Pega's assignment routing?
o: They bring members from different functional teams together to complete work that spans functions, reducing hand-off delays and improving efficiency
They replace SLAs with manual deadline tracking
They restrict assignments to a single named operator
They eliminate the need for any routing configuration
Mock Exam 2.r: Cross-functional Work Groups associate users and Work Queues from different teams under a manager, allowing work that spans functions to be handled efficiently without hand-off delays. They organize collaboration, not restrict it to one person.

Mock Exam 2.q: Which TWO statements correctly describe the relationship between a When Condition and a Decision Table in Case workflow?
o: A When Condition evaluates a true/false Boolean for a two-way branch in the Process Flow
A Decision Table maps condition combinations to specific outcomes for complex multi-way decisions
A When Condition handles multi-outcome routing better than a Decision Table
A Decision Table can only produce a true/false result
Mock Exam 2.r: When Conditions handle binary (true/false) branching; Decision Tables handle complex multi-outcome decisions by mapping condition combinations to specific return values (evaluated top-to-bottom, first match). They complement each other for different branching needs.

Mock Exam 2.q: A timer Wait Step in a Case Process pauses the Case until:
o: All child Cases reach Resolved status
A specific date and time is reached, after which the Case continues automatically
The SLA deadline passes
A user submits a form
Mock Exam 2.r: A timer Wait Step pauses the Case until a configured date/time, then continues automatically. A case-dependency Wait pauses until child Cases reach a status. User form submission is a Collect information Step; SLA expiry triggers urgency changes, not a Wait.

Mock Exam 2.q: A Data Transform copies billing address values into shipping address fields. Which use case does this represent?
o: Validating that a required field is not empty
Routing an Assignment to a Work Queue
Configuring an SLA goal interval
Copying data from one set of fields to another within or across Cases
Mock Exam 2.r: Data Transforms set, copy, and transform data values between pages and fields — including copying billing to shipping addresses. Validation rules check field correctness; routing and SLA configuration are separate capabilities.

Mock Exam 2.q: A default field value of 'Country = USA' is configured to pre-populate when a Case is created. What is the primary business benefit?
o: It prevents users from ever changing the country value
It reduces data entry time and errors by pre-filling commonly-used values so users only change them when needed
It routes the Case to a US-specific Work Queue
It validates that the country matches an external system
Mock Exam 2.r: Default values speed data entry and reduce errors by pre-populating commonly-used values; users override them when the situation differs. Defaults do not lock values, validate against external systems, or trigger routing.

Mock Exam 2.q: In a duplicate Case check, weighted conditions each carry a numeric score. The system flags a Case as a duplicate when:
o: The basic conditions fail but weighted scores are high enough
Only basic conditions must match; weighted conditions are ignored
All basic conditions match AND the sum of weighted condition scores meets or exceeds the configured threshold
Any weighted condition score alone exceeds the threshold
Mock Exam 2.r: Both must be met: all basic conditions MUST match (mandatory), AND the total weighted score must reach the configured threshold. Weighted conditions alone are not sufficient; basic conditions failing cannot be compensated by high weighted scores.

Mock Exam 2.q: A Persona in Pega Platform is best defined as:
o: A single named operator with a unique Operator ID
A set of Pega Platform rules that control data access
A Work Queue accessible to a specific team
A category of users who share similar access needs, goals, and UI requirements — representing the role a user plays
Mock Exam 2.r: A Persona is a category (role) of users with shared access needs and goals, not an individual user. An individual user is an operator with an Operator ID. Rules control platform behavior; Work Queues are routing constructs.

Mock Exam 2.q: Which Data Model level is built with business stakeholders using Entities, Attributes, and Relationships, describing WHAT data exists without specifying storage?
o: Conceptual Data Model
Physical Data Model
Logical Data Model
Visual Integration Map
Mock Exam 2.r: The Conceptual Data Model uses Entities, Attributes, and Relationships to describe WHAT data exists — built collaboratively with business stakeholders. The Logical model translates these to Pega data objects/fields; the Physical model addresses how data is stored and accessed.

Mock Exam 2.q: A data object created from the Case Life Cycle Designer without configuring fields or integration is called:
o: A Production data object
A simulated data source
A Draft data object
A Savable Data Page
Mock Exam 2.r: A Draft data object is a placeholder created when you add a data object in the Case Life Cycle Designer without configuring fields or integration settings. It must be fully configured before production use.

Mock Exam 2.q: An order can contain many products, each with a quantity entered by the user. The list of order lines is added to the order Case during processing. Which relationship type and cardinality should be configured for the order lines?
o: Embedded Data, List of records
Data reference, List of records
Case reference, List of records
Embedded Data, Single record
Mock Exam 2.r: User-entered data stored within the Case instance uses Embedded Data. Many order lines (one per product) means List of records cardinality. Data reference is for external/local SOR records; Case reference is for data from another Case Type.

Mock Exam 2.q: In Pega Platform, each locally-stored Data Record receives an automatically-assigned unique identifier. What is this identifier called?
o: Case ID
Operator ID
pyGUID
Ruleset version
Mock Exam 2.r: Each locally-stored Data Record gets a pyGUID — an auto-assigned unique identifier stored with the Case for later retrieval. The Case ID identifies the Case itself; Operator ID identifies the user; Ruleset version identifies a Rule package.

Mock Exam 2.q: A Savable Data Page is used to:
o: Cache data for read-only display in the application
Save updated data back to the system of record, both local and external
Generate sample data for testing
Create a new Case Type at runtime
Mock Exam 2.r: A Savable Data Page writes updated page data back to its system of record (local or external), enabling real-time updates. Standard read-only Data Pages cache data for display. Case Type creation and sample data generation are separate capabilities.

Mock Exam 2.q: Which TWO statements correctly describe the Visual Data Model's relationship cardinality indicators?
o: Multiple lines on one side of the connector represents a one-to-many relationship
Multiple lines on both sides means one-to-one
A single line on both sides of the connector represents a one-to-one relationship
A single line on both sides means many-to-many
Mock Exam 2.r: In the Visual Data Model: single line on both sides = one-to-one; multiple lines on one side = one-to-many; multiple lines on both sides = many-to-many. The other options invert or misstate these indicators.

Mock Exam 2.q: Which approach integrates with a legacy system that has no usable API when the integration must complete during a live customer call?
o: A standard API connector
Attended RPA — a robot drives the legacy UI in real time alongside the human operator
A Savable Data Page
Unattended RPA — queued for overnight background processing
Mock Exam 2.r: When no API is available and a human is in the process during the call, attended RPA drives the legacy system's UI in real time. Unattended RPA would defer the update; an API connector requires a supported protocol; a Savable Data Page saves local/external data but doesn't drive a legacy UI.

Mock Exam 2.q: Pega GenAI Knowledge Buddy is best described as:
o: A design-time assistant for generating Case Types in App Studio
A run-time tool that provides task-specific advice on an open Case
A standalone SaaS tool for designing new application workflows
A conversational tool that gives employees instant answers from the organization's own procedural documents and knowledge bases
Mock Exam 2.r: Knowledge Buddy combines Pega GenAI with the organization's procedural documents and knowledge bases to deliver instant conversational answers. Autopilot is the design-time assistant; Coach gives run-time Case-task advice; Blueprint is the standalone SaaS design tool.

Mock Exam 2.q: After configuring a Connect Generative AI Step's prompt and response mapping, what additional step is required so end users can see the AI-generated response?
o: Identify a target field and add it to the application's UI
Lock the Ruleset containing the Connect Step
Enable unattended RPA
Create an Access Role for the response
Mock Exam 2.r: You must identify a target field to receive the GenAI response and add that field to the UI so the response is visible to the user. Without a mapped target field and UI element, the output is inaccessible to the user.

Mock Exam 2.q: The Pega GenAI suite of features became available beginning with which Pega Infinity release?
o: Pega Platform 8.7
Pega Infinity '21
Pega Infinity '23
Pega Infinity '25 only
Mock Exam 2.r: Pega GenAI features — Blueprint, Autopilot, Coach, Knowledge Buddy, and Agents — became available beginning with Pega Infinity '23. Earlier versions do not include the GenAI feature suite.

Mock Exam 2.q: Which sequence correctly describes the Pega Blueprint end-to-end workflow?
o: Describe the app in business terms → Blueprint proposes design → team refines collaboratively → export and import into Pega to jumpstart development
Write Java code → compile → deploy Blueprint → export
Design in Dev Studio → export to Blueprint → share with stakeholders
Import Blueprint first → then describe the app → then refine
Mock Exam 2.r: The Blueprint workflow is: describe in business terms → AI proposes Case Types/Life Cycles/Data/Personas → team refines collaboratively → export/import into Pega to produce a functional application rapidly. The other sequences are invented or reversed.

Mock Exam 2.q: Which TWO are accurate statements about Pega GenAI Autopilot in Pega Infinity '23 and '24?
o: Autopilot features are inactive by default and require additional configuration to enable
Developers should review and modify Autopilot suggestions before accepting them, as Pega is not responsible for AI suggestion content
Pega guarantees the accuracy of all Autopilot-generated recommendations
Autopilot features are active by default with no additional setup
Mock Exam 2.r: In Pega Infinity '23 and '24, Autopilot is inactive by default and must be configured/enabled. Developers must review suggestions before accepting them (human-in-the-loop); Pega is not responsible for AI-generated content. The other options invert these facts.

Mock Exam 2.q: A Full Page View in Pega Platform is automatically added when:
o: A new Branch is merged to the target Ruleset
A Blueprint is imported into Pega Platform
A new Case Type or data object is created
A user logs into Admin Studio
Mock Exam 2.r: Pega automatically adds a Full Page View when a new Case Type or data object is created, providing the three-pane framework (navigation, summary panel, detail area) as the default workspace for a Case.

Mock Exam 2.q: Each Case Type supports exactly how many Promoted Actions, and where is it displayed?
o: One Promoted Action, displayed as a button on the Case header
Up to three Promoted Actions in the Summary panel
One Promoted Action per Stage, displayed in the Stage header
Unlimited Promoted Actions in the navigation pane
Mock Exam 2.r: Each Case Type supports exactly ONE Promoted Action — the first Case-wide Action — displayed as a button on the Case header. It provides quick access to a frequently used action without requiring a separate button component.

Mock Exam 2.q: The Summary panel in a Pega Full Page View is used to:
o: Collect user data entry for a Process Step
Configure the SLA goal and deadline
Display the most critical Case information in the upper-left pane, typically including Primary Fields for quick-glance status
Route an Assignment to the correct operator
Mock Exam 2.r: The Summary panel is the upper-left pane of the Full Page View, showing the most critical Case information (often Primary Fields) for at-a-glance status review. It is not a data-entry form, routing mechanism, or SLA configuration area.

Mock Exam 2.q: Among the four View types (Full Page, Partial, List, Form), which is the only one that is editable by default?
o: List
Form
Partial
Full Page
Mock Exam 2.r: Form Views are editable (designed for data collection with navigation buttons). Full Page and Partial Views are read-only. List Views are read-only by default but can optionally enable editing. Form is the primary data-collection View type.

Mock Exam 2.q: Which TWO statements correctly describe how Portals support user productivity in Pega?
o: Adding new landing pages and navigation entries lets a BA update a portal with new content areas
Portals are tailored by channel and Persona so each user type sees tools and information relevant to their role
Portals can only be configured in Dev Studio by System Architects
A single portal serves all users identically regardless of their role or channel
Mock Exam 2.r: Portals are tailored by Persona and channel for role-appropriate productivity, and they can be updated by adding landing pages and navigation entries. A single generic portal for all users defeats personalization; portals are configured in App Studio, not only Dev Studio.

Mock Exam 2.q: An Insight in Pega Platform is best described as:
o: A saved data query rendered as a table or chart that can be shared between users
A Ruleset that packages reusable UI components
A routing configuration that assigns Cases to Work Queues
A compliance rule that validates Case data against regulatory standards
Mock Exam 2.r: An Insight transforms a data query into a table or visualization (chart) that can be saved and shared, providing self-service operational analysis. It is not a compliance rule, Ruleset, or routing configuration.

Mock Exam 2.q: Which type of Insight is best for showing detailed row-level data, such as a list of open Claims Cases with key field values?
o: A Data Page
Chart Insight
Table Insight
BIX extraction
Mock Exam 2.r: A Table Insight presents query results as rows and columns — ideal for detailed, record-level review. A Chart Insight provides visual trend analysis; BIX extracts data to external BI tools; a Data Page retrieves and caches data but does not produce a report.

Mock Exam 2.q: BIX (Business Intelligence Exchange) is used when:
o: A BA creates a quick bar chart within App Studio
Operational dashboards are needed inside the Pega portal for real-time monitoring
Application data must be extracted from Pega into an external database or BI tool for large-scale or cross-system analytics
Data needs to be saved back to a system of record
Mock Exam 2.r: BIX is Pega's data extract capability for pulling data into external BI environments at scale. In-portal dashboards and quick bar charts use Insights; saving data back to a system of record uses Savable Data Pages.

Mock Exam 2.q: An Access Group in Pega Platform associates an operator with which set of items?
o: An application, a set of Access Roles, available Portals, and a default Work Group
A Blueprint, a Branch, and a Workspace
A Ruleset, a Data Page, and a simulated data source
A Case Type, a Stage, and a Process
Mock Exam 2.r: An Access Group associates an operator with an application, a set of Access Roles, the available Portals (studios), and a default Work Group. It is the key security and access configuration record linking an operator to their permissions and workspace.

Mock Exam 2.q: What is the correct order of the authentication and authorization processes in Pega Platform?
o: Authorization occurs first; authentication occurs after
Authentication (verifying identity) occurs first; authorization (determining permissions) occurs after
Authorization occurs only if the user fails authentication
They occur simultaneously with no defined order
Mock Exam 2.r: Authentication (verifying WHO the user is) always occurs first at login. Authorization (determining WHAT the authenticated user can access and do via Access Roles) happens after authentication succeeds. They are sequential, not simultaneous.

Mock Exam 3.q: A BA collaborates with Business and IT to design, build, and test a complaints management application, ensuring both sides understand requirements and the redesigned workflow. Which core BA responsibility is being performed?
o: Alignment
Analysis
Process Design
Education
Mock Exam 3.r: Alignment involves collaborating with both Business and IT to design, build, and test the solution. Education teaches OOTB value; Analysis diagnoses the current process; Process Design optimizes the workflow in Blueprint.

Mock Exam 3.q: Which App Studio navigation item provides a centralized repository of reusable assets for developers of all skill levels?
o: Library (Reuse Library)
Users
Channels
Overview
Mock Exam 3.r: The Library (Reuse Library) in App Studio is the centralized repository of reusable assets. Channels configures web/mobile portals; Users manages operators; Overview shows Case Types and Channels at a glance.

Mock Exam 3.q: The Solutions Consultant's role in a Pega project is best described as:
o: The Scrum Master equivalent who facilitates ceremonies
A quality analyst who builds test scripts from user stories
The person responsible for importing the Blueprint into Pega Platform
A pre-sales role who designs the Blueprint with client stakeholders and then transitions it to delivery BAs and SAs before the project begins
Mock Exam 3.r: The Solutions Consultant works during the sales phase, designs the Blueprint with the client, and transitions it to delivery BAs and SAs before delivery begins. The LSA imports the Blueprint; the Scrum Master facilitates ceremonies; QAs build test scripts.

Mock Exam 3.q: Omnichannel application reach in Pega means:
o: The same Pega application can serve as a web page, mobile app, or chatbot without maintaining separate code lines
Channel configuration requires Java coding in Dev Studio
A separate application must be built for each delivery channel
Only web channels are supported in App Studio
Mock Exam 3.r: Pega's low-code platform allows the same application to reach users across web, mobile, chatbot, and other channels without maintaining channel-specific code. This is a key value of the Center-out and low-code approach.

Mock Exam 3.q: Which TWO guiding principles of modular enterprise reuse are correctly defined?
o: Updateable — all components must be updated simultaneously across the entire application
Governed — governance is optional and provides no measurable value to the reuse program
Governed — a governance framework such as a Center of Excellence manages, evolves, and ensures quality of reusable assets
Updateable — individual components can be updated independently without disrupting the entire application
Mock Exam 3.r: Updateable means individual components update independently without disrupting the application; Governed means a Center of Excellence (or similar) manages and ensures asset quality. Simultaneous full-app updates and optional governance contradict both principles.

Mock Exam 3.q: An application class must inherit standard Pega Rules from the Work- class, which is outside its business class-name prefix hierarchy. Which inheritance type enables this?
o: Ruleset inheritance, via the Ruleset stack
Directed inheritance, specified explicitly on the class form
Pattern inheritance, which is automatic by class-name prefix
Multiple inheritance, combining both parent classes simultaneously
Mock Exam 3.r: Directed inheritance explicitly specifies a parent class on the class form, allowing a business class to inherit from standard Pega classes (such as Work-) outside the naming hierarchy. Pattern inheritance only follows the class-name prefix automatically.

Mock Exam 3.q: In the Center-out architecture, when an organization migrates its system of record from on-premises to the cloud, which layer is insulated from the change?
o: The application and business logic layer (center hub)
All three layers require changes
The data access layer
The presentation (channels) layer
Mock Exam 3.r: The data access layer connects DOWN to data in a way that insulates the central business logic from storage changes. Migrating from on-prem to cloud affects the data layer's configuration but not the application's business logic at the center.

Mock Exam 3.q: Which of the three class types in Pega Platform contains Rules that connect the application to external systems such as databases and web services?
o: Integration class
Work class
Data class
Access class
Mock Exam 3.r: The Integration class holds Rules that connect a Pega application to external systems (databases, web services, etc.). The Work class processes Cases; the Data class describes data types; 'Access class' is not a standard Pega class type.

Mock Exam 3.q: What is a key benefit of the low-code approach as used in Pega Platform?
o: It limits development to trivial, spreadsheet-level applications
It eliminates the need for any testing before deployment
It requires all contributors to have advanced Java programming skills
It creates a common visual language that enables business stakeholders and developers to collaborate more effectively
Mock Exam 3.r: Low-code creates a common visual language bridging business and IT, enabling faster, better-quality collaboration. It does not eliminate testing, is suitable for robust enterprise applications, and does not require Java from all contributors.

Mock Exam 3.q: Which TWO of the following correctly describe Pega Cloud deployment options?
o: Pega Cloud is a cloud-native platform that eliminates infrastructure management for organizations using a cloud deployment
Pega Cloud requires organizations to provision and manage all server hardware themselves
Pega Cloud is only available for small-scale applications with fewer than 10 users
Organizations can choose between Pega-managed cloud, client-managed cloud, or on-premise deployment (Cloud Choice)
Mock Exam 3.r: Pega Cloud is a cloud-native platform with Pega managing infrastructure. Cloud Choice gives organizations flexibility: Pega-managed cloud, client-managed cloud, or on-premise. Organizations on Pega Cloud do not manage their own hardware, and there is no user-count restriction.

Mock Exam 3.q: The Product Owner's primary responsibility in a Pega Scrum project is:
o: Facilitating Scrum ceremonies and removing blockers for the team
Importing the Blueprint and configuring functional requirements
Managing project scope and prioritizing the requirements backlog throughout development
Managing delivery governance, timeline, and budget
Mock Exam 3.r: The Product Owner manages scope and prioritizes the backlog. The Scrum Master facilitates ceremonies and removes blockers; the LSA imports/configures the Blueprint; the Project Delivery Lead (PDL) manages governance, timeline, and budget.

Mock Exam 3.q: What does Pega's Agile Workbench capture, and from where in the platform is it accessed?
o: Security role mappings — accessed from Admin Studio
Real-time feedback, user stories, bugs, and feature tracking — accessed from the App Studio header
SLA goal and deadline settings — accessed from the Case Life Cycle Designer
Decision Table configurations — accessed from the Rules library in Dev Studio
Mock Exam 3.r: Pega Agile Workbench captures real-time feedback and tracks feature development (stories, bugs) and is opened from the App Studio header. It is not for Decision Tables, SLA settings, or security configuration.

Mock Exam 3.q: Parametrization in the context of Pega Rules is used to:
o: Lock a Ruleset so no further changes can be made
Drive a Rule's logic based on a passed value instead of hard-coded data, reducing duplication and increasing reusability
Configure a SaaS connection to an external system
Define the access permissions for a role
Mock Exam 3.r: Parametrization passes values into a Rule to vary its logic dynamically, reducing code duplication and avoiding multiple near-identical Rule versions. It is not a locking, access, or integration configuration mechanism.

Mock Exam 3.q: Which Pega feature keeps all Case participants informed by allowing team members to post messages, comment, and reply in the context of a specific Case?
o: Agile Workbench
Insights
Pulse
Tags
Mock Exam 3.r: Pulse is the in-context collaboration feed for posting, commenting, and replying within a Case. Agile Workbench tracks stories and feedback; Insights analyze data; Tags label items for organization and discovery.

Mock Exam 3.q: A Step in a Case Process requires a user to enter customer contact details. Which icon color denotes this Step type in App Studio?
o: Red — Collect information Steps end the lifecycle
Blue — Collect information Steps route to Work Queues
Yellow — Collect information Steps are automated
Green — Collect information Steps require user action
Mock Exam 3.r: Collect information Steps (user-action Steps) are displayed with green icons. Yellow icons indicate Automation Steps (system-executed). Red indicates Resolution Stage bars, not Step icons. Blue is not a standard Step icon color.

Mock Exam 3.q: A calculated value field in Pega Platform is best described as:
o: A field computed automatically from an expression referencing other fields, recalculated as input fields change, and typically read-only
A field that validates input against a fixed picklist
A field populated by a Data Transform at Case creation only
A field that the user must type into manually each time
Mock Exam 3.r: A calculated value field is auto-computed from an expression referencing other fields; the system owns the value and recalculates it as inputs change. Users cannot edit it directly. Picklists validate fixed options; Data Transforms are used for seeding values, not continuous calculation.

Mock Exam 3.q: A BA is naming a new Case Type for a travel insurance claims process. Which name follows Pega naming conventions for Case Types?
o: Travel Insurance Claim
ClaimProcess1
Processing
Submit claim
Mock Exam 3.r: Case Type names are outcome-focused noun phrases that clearly convey the purpose of the process (e.g., 'Travel Insurance Claim'). 'Processing' is a Stage-style name; 'Submit claim' is a verb+noun Step/Process name; 'ClaimProcess1' is a non-descriptive technical identifier.

Mock Exam 3.q: Which TWO of the following correctly describe the three pillars used to capture a Microjourney in App Studio?
o: Rulesets and Versions define the three pillars
Data and Interfaces describe the information needed and how it is accessed
Case Types and Strategies define the Case Life Cycle and how work is processed
SLAs and Urgency define the three pillars
Mock Exam 3.r: The three pillars of a Pega application's Microjourney are Case Types & Strategies (the Life Cycle), Data & Interfaces (the information model), and Personas & Channels (who interacts and how). Rulesets/Versions and SLAs are not among the three pillars.

Mock Exam 3.q: When an App Studio Process's 'Allow users to go back to the previous Step' option is enabled, what appears in the user interface at runtime?
o: A Skip button that bypasses the current Step
A Previous button that lets users navigate to the prior Step
A Change Stage button in the Case header
A Resolve button that ends the Case
Mock Exam 3.r: Enabling 'Allow users to go back to the previous Step' on a Process adds a Previous button at runtime. By default, only Submit (forward) is shown. Resolve, Skip, and Change Stage buttons are separate, unrelated UI options.

Mock Exam 3.q: A BA configures a bypass so a Stage is skipped when a specific condition is true. Which App Studio capability enables this?
o: A parallel Process configuration
A Savable Data Page
A When Condition applied to the Stage that bypasses it when the condition evaluates to true
A Change Stage Automation Step
Mock Exam 3.r: Applying a When Condition to a Stage or Process configures conditional bypassing — the Case skips the Stage when the condition is true. A Change Stage Automation explicitly transitions to a named Stage; parallel Processes are for concurrent work; Savable Data Pages save data.

Mock Exam 3.q: Which description best defines a Service-Level Agreement (SLA) goal interval?
o: The earlier target by which an Assignment SHOULD be completed
The initial urgency value assigned when a Case is created
The later hard limit by which an Assignment MUST be completed
The time interval between reminder notifications
Mock Exam 3.r: The SLA Goal is the earlier 'should-complete-by' target. The Deadline is the later 'must-complete-by' hard limit. Both thresholds, when passed, automatically increase Case Urgency. The initial urgency value is set separately; reminder intervals are configurable in Dev Studio.

Mock Exam 3.q: When a child Case is created automatically within a parent Case's workflow, which Step type is used?
o: A Change Stage Automation Step
A Wait Step (case-dependency)
A Collect information Step
A Create Case Automation Step
Mock Exam 3.r: A Create Case Automation Step automatically creates a child Case within the parent's Process Flow. Collect information Steps require user input; Wait Steps pause execution; Change Stage Steps transition between Stages.

Mock Exam 3.q: The primary path in a Case Life Cycle refers to:
o: Any path that includes at least one Alternate Stage
The first Stage in the Case Life Cycle
The path through the Life Cycle following only Primary Stages, leading to the expected positive resolution
The path configured in the Create Stage
Mock Exam 3.r: The primary path is the route through the Case Life Cycle that follows only Primary Stages toward an expected positive resolution outcome. Alternate Stages are deviations from this path. The Create Stage is always first regardless of which path.

Mock Exam 3.q: Which TWO are valid examples of what an Automation Step (yellow icon) can do within a Pega Process Flow?
o: Create a PDF document automatically
Collect required data input from the case worker
Wait a specified duration before continuing the Case
Display an approval form to the manager
Mock Exam 3.r: Automation Steps (yellow icons) perform system-executed actions: create PDFs, send emails, wait for a duration, change Stage, or create child Cases. Collecting user input and displaying forms are Collect information Steps (green icons).

Mock Exam 3.q: A shipping cost is determined by destination region and package weight with multiple possible outcomes. Which rule type is best for this multi-condition calculation?
o: Decision Table
Data Transform
When Condition
Calculated value field with a single expression
Mock Exam 3.r: A Decision Table maps multiple condition combinations (region × weight) to a specific outcome (shipping cost), evaluated top-to-bottom with first-match logic. A When Condition handles only true/false binary branching; Data Transforms set/copy values; a single expression field works only for simple formulas.

Mock Exam 3.q: In a duplicate Case check, if basic conditions do not match, what happens to the weighted condition scoring?
o: The system prompts the user to verify the basic conditions manually
The Case is not flagged regardless of weighted scores, because basic conditions must all match first
The Case is immediately resolved as a duplicate
The weighted scores are still summed and the threshold checked independently
Mock Exam 3.r: Basic conditions are mandatory — ALL must match before weighted conditions are evaluated. If any basic condition fails, the Case is not flagged as a potential duplicate regardless of how high the weighted scores might be.

Mock Exam 3.q: A Work Group in Pega Platform is used to:
o: Configure the Case Life Cycle Stages and Processes
Define the permissions a user has for accessing specific Classes and rules
Associate a set of users and Work Queues under a manager for coordinated collaboration across functional areas
Specify the SLA goal and deadline intervals for an Assignment
Mock Exam 3.r: A Work Group associates users and Work Queues under a manager, enabling coordinated cross-functional work. Access Roles define permissions; the Case Life Cycle designer configures Stages/Processes; SLA rules define goal/deadline intervals.

Mock Exam 3.q: Configuring a default property value is most valuable when:
o: The field value is sourced from an external system of record
The field is a calculated value derived from other fields
A field must always be left blank for user input
A field value is the same for most Cases and saving users from re-entering it each time speeds processing
Mock Exam 3.r: Default values are most valuable for commonly-used values that rarely change (e.g., Country = USA), saving users time. Blank mandatory fields need user input; calculated values are derived automatically; external SOR values come from Data references.

Mock Exam 3.q: At what level is a Conceptual Data Model built, and with whom?
o: By the Lead System Architect, using integration connectors and SOR configurations
With business stakeholders, using Entities, Attributes, and Relationships to describe WHAT data exists without addressing how it is stored
By System Architects in Dev Studio, using data types and properties
By the BA alone in App Studio, using data objects and fields
Mock Exam 3.r: The Conceptual Data Model is a living document built collaboratively with business stakeholders using Entities, Attributes, and Relationships. It describes WHAT data exists without technical storage details. The Logical model uses data objects/fields in App Studio; the Physical model addresses SOR configuration.

Mock Exam 3.q: An external product catalog integration is not yet available, but the team needs to continue building and testing. Which Data Page capability supports this?
o: A Savable Data Page that writes back to the external system
A Draft data object with no fields configured
Simulated data source — returns placeholder data from a temporary source while the real integration is built
A Case reference relationship pointing to a test Case
Mock Exam 3.r: Simulated data sources return placeholder data (e.g., from the Pega database) while the production integration is being developed, keeping the team unblocked. Savable Data Pages write back; Draft objects are placeholders without fields; Case references source data from other Case Types.

Mock Exam 3.q: The deciding factor between using Embedded Data and a Data reference for a data relationship is:
o: The Case Type: parent Cases use Embedded; child Cases use Data reference
The cardinality: Single record uses Embedded Data; List of records uses Data reference
The source of the data: Embedded Data is for user input directly in the Case; Data reference is for records from a local or external system of record
Whether the data object has a pyGUID: objects with pyGUID use Embedded; others use Data reference
Mock Exam 3.r: The source determines the relationship type: Embedded Data = typed directly into the Case instance; Data reference = from Data Records stored locally in Pega or retrieved from an external SOR. Cardinality (Single vs. List) is an independent, secondary decision.

Mock Exam 3.q: A shipping field requires users to choose from three fixed options: Standard, Express, or Overnight. Which Field Type enforces this closed set?
o: Attachment
Text
Boolean
Picklist
Mock Exam 3.r: A Picklist enforces a defined, closed set of valid options — preventing free-form text entries that could introduce inconsistency. Text allows any input; Boolean is yes/no; Attachment is for uploaded files.

Mock Exam 3.q: Which TWO statements correctly describe the difference between a data object (App Studio) and a data type (Dev Studio)?
o: A field in App Studio is called a property in Dev Studio — same structure, different name
A data type in Dev Studio has a fundamentally different structure from an App Studio data object
A data object is only visible in App Studio and cannot be opened in Dev Studio
A data object in App Studio is the same construct as a data type in Dev Studio — only the terminology differs
Mock Exam 3.r: Data object (App Studio) = data type (Dev Studio); Field (App Studio) = property (Dev Studio). The underlying structures are identical. Data objects created in App Studio are fully accessible and equivalent in Dev Studio.

Mock Exam 3.q: A data relationship does NOT store data itself. Its role is to:
o: Store the actual field values for each Case instance
Associate related fields to describe how data connects between a data object, a Case Type, or another Case Type
Define the physical database schema for Pega data tables
Replace the need for Data Pages when sourcing data
Mock Exam 3.r: A data relationship is a structural container describing how data connects between entities — it does NOT store data. The data lives in the fields of connected data objects. It is not a database schema definition and does not replace Data Pages.

Mock Exam 3.q: Pega Live Data is best described as:
o: A type of simulated data object used only during testing
A compliance certification for data security in Pega applications
A reporting tool for generating Insights from application data
A virtualization layer that separates business logic from the technical details of how and where data is accessed, with Data Pages as a key component
Mock Exam 3.r: Pega Live Data is the virtualization layer that separates business logic from storage/access details, with Data Pages serving as the key bridge. It is not a reporting tool, security certification, or test-only mechanism.

Mock Exam 3.q: Pega GenAI Coach is designed to help which group, and at what point in the application lifecycle?
o: End users at runtime — providing expert, task-specific advice on their current Case or assignment
Developers at design time — suggesting Case Type workflows and Data Model fields
Business Analysts at the sales phase — designing the initial Blueprint
System Architects at deployment time — automating the CI/CD pipeline
Mock Exam 3.r: Pega GenAI Coach provides expert advice and feedback to END USERS on their tasks at APPLICATION RUNTIME. Autopilot and Blueprint help at design time; Deployment Manager handles CI/CD; the Solutions Consultant uses Blueprint in the sales phase.

Mock Exam 3.q: A Connect Generative AI Step returns a list of items (e.g., required documents) that maps to an embedded page list in the Data Model. Which response structure should be selected?
o: Encrypted - Binary
Unstructured
Structured - Single
Structured - List
Mock Exam 3.r: Structured-List maps multiple AI-returned objects to an embedded page list — ideal for a list of required documents. Structured-Single is for a single object/field; Unstructured maps raw text to a Text paragraph field; Encrypted-Binary is not a valid response structure.

Mock Exam 3.q: Where is a Pega Blueprint created?
o: At pega.com/blueprint — a standalone SaaS website separate from Pega Platform
In App Studio's Library section
In Admin Studio's monitoring dashboard
In Dev Studio's Records tab
Mock Exam 3.r: Blueprints are created at pega.com/blueprint, confirming Blueprint's nature as a standalone SaaS tool separate from Pega Platform's studios. It is not embedded in App Studio, Dev Studio, or Admin Studio.

Mock Exam 3.q: Which TWO correctly describe Pega GenAI Agents governed by Tool Rules?
o: Tool Rules provide guardrails, governance, and security compliance for what an Agent is permitted to do
Agents operate at design time only and cannot interact with running Cases
Agents replace the need for any security or compliance controls in the application
Agents can run automations, start Cases, and call other agents at run time
Mock Exam 3.r: Agents automate Case processing at run time (run automations, start Cases, call other agents, etc.). Tool Rules govern what Agents can do, adding security and compliance guardrails. Agents do not replace security; they operate at run time, not only design time.

Mock Exam 3.q: A Connect Generative AI Step's response masking capability is useful when:
o: Sensitive data must be protected during the LLM request and response cycle
The step is used at design time rather than run time
The response is structured as a single object mapped to one field
The AI response needs to be displayed in multiple languages simultaneously
Mock Exam 3.r: Connect Rules can mask sensitive data during the GenAI request/response cycle — for example, preventing PII from being sent to or returned from the LLM. Language localization is also supported (changing response language based on user locale) but is a different capability.

Mock Exam 3.q: A View configured from a Workflow tab Step's 'Configure View' button is automatically created using which template?
o: No template — it is created blank
The Default template
A custom template specified by the BA
The Cascading template
Mock Exam 3.r: When clicking 'Configure View' on a Step in the Workflow tab, Pega auto-creates a Form View using the Default template. Views created in the UX tab (manual creation) are not auto-generated. Custom templates are available but are not the auto-created choice.

Mock Exam 3.q: The Pega UI design principle that ensures each front-end component has a single responsibility and is decoupled from back-end APIs is:
o: Model-driven UI
Pattern-based inheritance
Separation of Concerns
Situational Layer Cake
Mock Exam 3.r: Separation of Concerns divides the application into distinct, single-responsibility parts so the UI is decoupled from business logic and APIs. Model-driven UI generates interface from data models; Pattern-based inheritance and the Situational Layer Cake are architecture and reuse concepts.

Mock Exam 3.q: When a BA tailors a portal for a customer-service representative (CSR) persona so they see only the work queues and quick-action buttons relevant to their role, which benefit is being realized?
o: Removal of the Summary panel from all Case Type views
Reduced application security for that persona's access group
A role-appropriate, productive experience that improves efficiency and the user experience
Elimination of Landing Pages from the portal
Mock Exam 3.r: Tailoring portals by Persona ensures each user type (e.g., CSR) sees a role-appropriate workspace with relevant tools and information, improving efficiency and the user experience. Tailoring does not affect security settings, remove Summary panels, or eliminate Landing Pages.

Mock Exam 3.q: Which TWO View types in Pega Platform are read-only by default?
o: Form View — designed for collecting user input (editable by design)
Partial View — displays a subset of Case information in read-only mode
List View with inline editing enabled — configured to allow record-level edits
Full Page View — provides the three-pane workspace framework for a Case
Mock Exam 3.r: Full Page Views and Partial Views are read-only by default. Form Views are editable by design (data collection). List Views are read-only by default but can be configured to allow inline editing — so a List View with inline editing enabled is no longer read-only.

Mock Exam 3.q: Dynamic visibility in a Pega View allows a BA to:
o: Lock a Ruleset after the View configuration is complete
Route an Assignment to a Work Queue based on field values
Change the color of a field's value when it exceeds a threshold
Show or hide a field or UI element based on a runtime condition
Mock Exam 3.r: Dynamic visibility controls whether UI elements are shown or hidden at run time based on conditions. Changing colors is conditional formatting; routing based on field values is an Assignment configuration; Ruleset locking is a deployment/governance action.

Mock Exam 3.q: What are the two output formats available when saving an Insight in Pega Platform?
o: A Wait Step or an SLA
A table (rows and columns) or a chart (visualization such as bar, line, or pie)
A Ruleset or an Access Role
A Process Flow or a Decision Table
Mock Exam 3.r: An Insight renders a saved data query as either a table (rows/columns for detail review) or a chart/visualization (for trend analysis). Rulesets, Access Roles, Process Flows, Decision Tables, Wait Steps, and SLAs are not Insight output formats.

Mock Exam 3.q: A team manager needs a quick visualization of how many Claims Cases were opened each day for the past 30 days to identify processing peaks. Which Insight type is most appropriate?
o: A Chart Insight (e.g., bar or line chart) showing Cases opened per day
A Savable Data Page that writes Cases back to the SOR
BIX extraction to an external data warehouse
A Table Insight listing every Case opened in the period with all fields
Mock Exam 3.r: A Chart Insight visualizes trends (e.g., Cases per day) at a glance — perfect for identifying peaks. A Table Insight is for detailed record-level review; BIX is for external extraction at scale; Savable Data Pages are for writing data back to sources.

Mock Exam 3.q: The Explore Data landing page in App Studio is used for:
o: Configuring the Case Life Cycle Stages and Processes
Managing Operator records and Access Groups
Accessing Insights and building data queries to analyze application data and monitor team and process performance
Configuring integrations to external systems of record
Mock Exam 3.r: The Explore Data landing page is the dedicated area in App Studio for analyzing application data and building Insights. Integration configuration is in Data & Interfaces; Operator/Access Group management is in Users and Admin Studio; Case Life Cycle design is in the Case Type designer.

Mock Exam 3.q: In Pega Platform, each individual user is represented by an Operator record. What does an Operator record store?
o: The user's Ruleset versions and Branch configurations
The user's Work Queue assignments and SLA urgency values
The user's Decision Tables and When Conditions
The user's profile and credentials, and a link to their Access Group
Mock Exam 3.r: An Operator record stores the user's profile and credentials and links them to their Access Group — which determines the application, portals, roles, and default Work Group the user receives. Work Queues, Decision Tables, and Rulesets are not stored in the Operator record.

Mock Exam 3.q: Which TWO statements about authentication and authorization in Pega Platform are correct?
o: Authorization occurs before authentication in Pega's security model
Authentication verifies the user's identity at login and occurs before authorization
Authentication determines what rules and Case Types a user can access
Authorization uses Access Roles and Access Groups to determine what an authenticated user is permitted to do
Mock Exam 3.r: Authentication verifies identity first (at login). Authorization then determines permitted actions via Access Roles/Groups. The order is always authentication first, authorization second. Authentication verifies identity, not rule/Case Type access — that is authorization's role.

Mock Exam 1.q: In HTML applications, what is the function of the ActionMode "Constraint"?
o: It defines the number of repetitions in a TestCase Folder
It limits the search for a particular control
It limits the number of TestSteps you can have in a TestStep Folder
It controls the number of constraints you can set in a TestCase
Mock Exam 1.r: ActionMode Constraint limits the search within a table/list to identify one specific control, regardless of where it sits — e.g., constraining on Product='Music 2' AND Price='*10.00*' to find that exact row. It does not define repetitions (that's the TestStepFolder 'Repetition' attribute), limit TestStep counts, or control the number of constraints — those are invented distractors.

Mock Exam 1.q: In a table, the cell that is being worked on is identified by using:
o: Identify by Anchor
SQL
Row and Column
Translate Value
Mock Exam 1.r: A table cell in Tosca is identified through the Row and Column hierarchy (<Row> then <Cell>). Identify by Anchor is a general control-identification technique unrelated to table steering specifically; SQL is irrelevant; Translate Value is a right-click feature to test an expression, not a cell-identification method.

Mock Exam 1.q: What happens to the results generated from trial runs in the ScratchBook?
o: They are temporary and will be overwritten when a new TestCase or TestStep is run
They are automatically saved as a new TestCase version
They are saved permanently unless manually deleted
They are stored in the TestCase folder for future reference
Mock Exam 1.r: ScratchBook results are temporary — each new run overwrites the previous one, and nothing is kept permanently. This is the key contrast with ExecutionLists, which store all historic results via the ActualLog. ScratchBook does not create TestCase versions or store results in the TestCase folder.

Mock Exam 1.q: What is the best practice for using Reusable TestStepBlocks in Tosca?
o: Reusable TestStepBlocks should be applied only for TestSteps that are part of Recovery Scenarios
Use them only for TestSteps or sequences of TestSteps that are needed more than once in your tests
Use Reusable TestStepBlocks when TestSteps or sequences of TestSteps are required multiple times across different TestCases
Reusable TestStepBlocks are valuable even for TestSteps that are needed just once
Mock Exam 1.r: The defining purpose of a Reusable TestStepBlock (Library) is to share a sequence — like a Login flow — across DIFFERENT TestCases, avoiding duplication. Recovery Scenarios are unrelated. A vaguer 'needed more than once in your tests' doesn't capture the cross-TestCase reuse that makes RTSBs valuable, and using them for steps needed just once adds unnecessary overhead.

Mock Exam 1.q: How can you reuse a randomly generated value in Tosca?
o: Add [*2] to the command to reuse the value
It is not possible to reuse a randomly generated value
Repeat the command and the same value will be generated again
Buffer the value after its initial creation to use it again
Mock Exam 1.r: Random-value expressions like {RND[..]} or {RANDOMTEXT[..]} generate a NEW value every time they are evaluated. To reuse the same generated value elsewhere, you must Buffer it at creation (ActionMode Buffer) and then recall it with {B[BufferName]}. Repeating the command generates a different value, not the same one, and '[*2]' is not valid Tosca syntax.

Mock Exam 1.q: What is the purpose of Conditions in Tosca?
o: To instruct Tosca on which TestSheet to run
To instruct Tosca on when to use, or not to use, certain elements within a TestCase
To provide a status report on the completion of the RequirementSet
To configure TestCase execution settings
Mock Exam 1.r: Conditions tell Tosca when to use (or not use) certain TestStepFolders, TestSteps, or TestStepValues within a TestCase — letting one Template cover multiple test paths. They don't select which TestSheet runs, report RequirementSet status, or configure general execution settings.

Mock Exam 1.q: What is the correct process to link a TestSheet to a Template?
o: Drag the TestSheet and drop it onto the TemplateInstances
Drag and drop the TestSheet onto the Template
Right click on the Template, select Instantiation, choose the TestSheet
Right click on the TestSheet and select the correct Template from the list
Mock Exam 1.r: You select the TestSheet in the TestCaseDesign section, then drag and drop it directly onto the Template in the TestCase section. TemplateInstances don't exist yet at this point (they're created by Instantiation), and there's no such Instantiation/list-based linking menu.

Mock Exam 1.q: Which of the following actions can you perform when managing ExecutionLists in Tosca? (two correct answers)
o: Drag the entire TemplateInstance folder into the ExecutionList
Manually adjust each TestCase in the ExecutionList
Create a new ExecutionList for each individual TestCase
Use the synchronize function to update the ExecutionList
Mock Exam 1.r: Best practice is to drag the whole TemplateInstance folder onto the ExecutionList (not individual TestCases), then use the manually-triggered synchronize function on the ExecutionList ribbon to update it whenever the Template changes. Manually adjusting each TestCase, or creating a separate ExecutionList per TestCase, is exactly the high-maintenance approach this workflow avoids.
